title: Match Nova's 16 px terminal typography
description:
## Observable contract

Consumer: a local user opening an unconfigured Venus terminal through Eon or EonTerm.

Trigger: Venus creates its default terminal grid at any supported display scale.

Result: terminal text uses a nominal 16 logical-pixel font size, matching Nova's selected size. The default row remains 18 logical pixels at 1x, giving an effective 1.125 line-height ratio—the integer-grid equivalent of Nova's configured 1.12 (16 × 1.12 = 17.92). Rendering, resize, pointer mapping, selection, cursor placement, IME, and accessibility consume the same scaled cell metrics.

Important failures: the horizontal fitting path must not silently reduce the selected face back to the current 14 px result; complete glyph ink must remain inside its row; adjacent rows must not overlap; grid capacity and cursor alignment remain coherent.

## Contract routing

Harden proved VEN-C1 and VEN-C2 while preserving VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, VEN-C9, and VEN-C13. Consume the current accepted Orbit presentation contract unchanged. This changes only Venus's no-profile fallback; it adds no public setting, protocol value, dependency, or Eon/Orbit behavior.

## Evidence and ownership

- Venus currently hardcodes CellMetrics at 9 × 18 logical pixels with nominal font_size 14 in src/render.rs.
- Nova defaults/mars/config.toml selects JetBrains Mono size 16.0 and line-height 1.12.
- Venus fitted_cell_font may reduce font size to preserve the fixed cell width, so changing only the 14 literal is not sufficient proof of the requested result.
- Venus owns native font fitting and grid materialization. Eon owns future product configuration and persistence.

Existing deferred bead ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7 owns configurable font family, size, and line-height materialization. Eon bead eon-eonterm-presentation-e4f owns the matching persisted product configuration. This issue does not duplicate or activate those broader settings surfaces.

## Minimum implementation

1. Write one focused metric/font-fit regression that fails on the current 14 px fallback and proves the selected default is actually laid out at 16 logical pixels at 1x, 1.25x, 1.5x, and 2x.
2. Keep the row height at 18 logical pixels. Adjust the default cell width only if the packaged monospace face otherwise forces fitted_cell_font below 16; use the smallest coherent metric change.
3. Reuse CellMetrics, fitted_cell_font, and every existing geometry consumer. Add no setting parser, profile type, module, dependency, font package, or second metric owner.
4. Reprove complete regular/bold/italic descenders, box and Braille alignment, wide/combining cells, cursor/input/selection geometry, resize, IME, accessibility, and canonical scenes.
5. Dogfood installed EonTerm/Eonova beside Nova on the same display scale and obtain user acceptance.

## Acceptance

- Default Venus uses an effective 16 logical-pixel terminal font at 1x and scales consistently at 1.25x, 1.5x, and 2x.
- Default row height remains 18 logical pixels at 1x; no separate line-height setting or approximation layer is added.
- Horizontal fitting does not undo the requested size. Any width change is derived once in CellMetrics and shared by rendering and interaction geometry.
- Complete glyph ink stays within row and pane clips with no overlap; existing typography, cursor, input, resize, IME, accessibility, and scene checks remain green.
- Native side-by-side Eon/EonTerm and Nova dogfood confirms the requested perceived size.
- Update VEN-C1/VEN-C2 proof metadata after an immutable source commit, CHANGELOG for the accepted visual default, and README LOC accounting.
- cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check all pass.

## Scope boundary and stop conditions

No configurable typography, family change, font packaging, live reload, opacity, geometry preference, renderer replacement, dependency, Orbit/Eon edit, or macOS claim. Stop for user approval if correct 16 px rendering requires a font-package change, a public setting, a new dependency, weakened clipping, or a contract beyond the stated hardening. Rebaseline if another active issue changes src/render.rs or CellMetrics.
notes: Accepted source: 846daf8fb7846b0e8dc227e533aa8d51a691f76f. Existing CellMetrics and fitted_cell_font remain the single geometry and font-fit owners: 10x18 logical cells, nominal 16 px text, and shared rendering/input/resize/IME/accessibility metrics. Rejected settings, font-package or dependency changes, a second metric owner, weakened clipping, and renderer replacement. Dependency footprint unchanged; Rust diff is +48/-18 across the existing renderer and host regression surfaces. Exact checks: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked; cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; git diff --check. Native isolated EonTerm with exact packaged Fontconfig passed, and user visual acceptance was received 2026-08-12. Remaining limits: configurable typography stays deferred; fractional/HiDPI native compositor quality and macOS remain unproved.
close_reason: User accepted the published 16 px candidate as much more readable and better looking; VEN-C1/VEN-C2 now name immutable proof 846daf8fb7846b0e8dc227e533aa8d51a691f76f.

title: Modularize Venus native host behind a thin main
description:
## Contract routing

This planning container reorganizes Venus internal Rust ownership without changing any current contract: VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, VEN-C7 through VEN-C11, and VEN-C13 through VEN-C16. It preserves canonical ORBS v4 at Orbit proof `7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c`, EONW v1 at Eon proof `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`, and Linux native-Wayland/Vulkan-only VEN-C16 at Venus proof `e033efadf023492ae02eb1e9036de98ad93d2f98`. This is an internal ownership move, not a contract, protocol, platform, or packaging change.

## Current source map

At accepted edge `fa96d8159511019f273b1cc32cf9e8661cab0d78`, `src/main.rs` is 2,411 lines:

- Launch values and validation are `DEFAULT_CURSOR_TAIL` and `USAGE` at lines 52-60, `LaunchArguments`, argument parsing, cursor-color parsing, and default socket selection at lines 1541-1653 and 1674-1685, with the focused launch test at lines 1734-1900.
- The concrete native host is `OrbitRetry`, presentation/window/application state, `UserEvent`, `Application`, `ApplicationHandler`, and directly coupled host helpers at lines 62-1524.
- Supervised presentation-control mechanics are at lines 1655-1672 and their focused test is at lines 1961-1975; they emit application-owned `UserEvent` values.
- Executable orchestration is at lines 1526-1538.

These line anchors document the current baseline; named owners and behavior govern if lines drift.

## Selected ownership and sequence

1. `ven-12v.1` extracts CLI values, validation, default socket/color policy, and the private supervision activation decision to `src/launch.rs`. It does not move the stdin reader or winit event routing.
2. `ven-12v.2` extracts the concrete winit application, event loop, native host helpers, and presentation-control mechanics to `src/application.rs`, consuming the validated launch value.
3. `src/main.rs` retains only module declarations, the crate result boundary, Linux-only compile guard, argument collection, and one call composing launch with application run.

Presentation-control mechanics stay with the application because they emit `UserEvent::Present` and `UserEvent::Exit`. Putting them in launch would require a reverse dependency or a second command abstraction. Keep one concrete application and one concrete validated launch value.

## Scope

In scope:
- the dependency-ordered child issues
- moving existing behavior and directly coupled tests to the two concrete owners
- preserving all arguments, environment semantics, defaults, errors, native event ordering, clipboard behavior, protocol bytes, rendering, input, accessibility, and lifecycle
- updating module declarations, internal visibility, proof metadata, and README LOC only as required by the moves

Out of scope:
- behavior changes, new contracts, public modules, dependencies, platform work, Eon or Orbit edits, and packaging
- opportunistic Linux-only cleanup unrelated to the move
- splitting `render.rs` or another established subsystem solely by size
- traits, factories, service containers, event buses, command adapters, or compatibility layers

## Success criteria

- `launch.rs` solely owns validated startup values and supervision selection.
- `application.rs` solely owns native application/window state, winit event composition, and presentation-control mechanics.
- Existing subsystem modules remain authoritative; neither new module copies their policy.
- `main.rs` is a thin executable composition boundary.
- Each child closes against an immutable source commit and the final sequence passes one complete unchanged-candidate Rust proof plus bounded native Wayland and absent-Wayland outer observations. Eon owns any later Nix/profile/package acceptance; this repository does not claim that proof.

## Reference gate

Required before each child: current `AGENTS.md`, this batch, affected VEN contracts, exact current `src/main.rs` and tests, and the accepted ORBS/EONW revisions above. Exact winit `fb45fbf901fbe70cc9a877b5d651d0b60c206b08` is required for the application child because it defines the event-loop owner. Monstar `71e4babde8e47e0739abd610f2afe202c8e99c00` remains comparison-only and is explicitly rejected as thin-main, PTY, terminal, renderer, or application-owner authority. No crate gate is expected.

## Stop conditions

Stop if a split changes observable behavior, requires a public surface or dependency, duplicates an existing subsystem owner, weakens VEN-C16, or only improves a line-count metric.
notes: Completed by accepted child source proofs `bab89d1a31bdb7a6a5985f12443f1ace3b0d7f18` and `8e506a247af7ce031798e198e691ca64671b5c27`, with proof metadata through `c0a1813b54daecda8fe9f1d085edd289eddbc301`. Fresh-eyes and ruthless isomorphic simplification review found no source correction that clears the ownership and behavior-preservation gates. The final 19-line main, private launch owner, private application owner, complete locked Rust proof, and bounded native observations satisfy every success criterion.
close_reason: Both ownership children are accepted and the fresh-eyes/simplification pass confirms every parent success criterion

- Fresh-eyes finding: the implementation and proof are complete, but this parent remained open after both children closed. `bv --robot-triage --format toon` identifies `ven-12v` as the sole open actionable issue; closing it is the only confirmed correction.
- Exact accepted sequence: launch owner source `bab89d1a31bdb7a6a5985f12443f1ace3b0d7f18`; application owner source `8e506a247af7ce031798e198e691ca64671b5c27`; proof metadata through `c0a1813b54daecda8fe9f1d085edd289eddbc301`. Root `src/main.rs` is 19 lines; `launch.rs` solely owns validation/defaults/supervision selection; `application.rs` solely owns winit lifecycle, native host state/events, and presentation control.
- Fresh unchanged-source verification passes `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, 59 library + 27 host + 14 canonical integration tests, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `git diff --check`. The child records the accepted absent-Wayland and isolated native-Wayland observations; AP-PROOF reuses those exact unchanged-source observations.
- Isomorphism/rejection ledger: inlining `application::run` into `main` saves no concept and violates the selected lifecycle owner; nesting launch under application or parsing there merges independent owners; moving the shared Result alias duplicates or broadens error policy; splitting the 2,130-line concrete host adds a product module solely by size. Each has zero concept reduction or fails the ownership/scope row, so no source edit clears the proof gate.
- Checked and acceptable: outputs, error text/status, event order, side effects, validation, ORBS/EONW bytes, timers/retries, thread/socket lifecycle, native platform boundary, tests, dependencies, and subsystem ownership are unchanged. README LOC is exact at 10,235 Rust source and 12,310 tracked total. A full second reasoning pass found no actionable source bug, DRY opportunity, or simplification.

title: Extract Venus launch and supervision policy
description:
## Contract routing

Preserve VEN-C1 cursor-profile defaults, VEN-C9 launch and decoration behavior, VEN-C11 opacity validation, VEN-C14 supervision activation, VEN-C15 blur validation, and VEN-C16 Linux native-Wayland-only startup. Preserve canonical ORBS v4 at `7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c` and EONW v1 at `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`; neither protocol changes. Portability disposition: neutral internal move whose output is consumed by the isolated Wayland application owner.

## Outcome and current source

Extract one binary-private `src/launch.rs` owner for validated startup values. At edge `fa96d8159511019f273b1cc32cf9e8661cab0d78`, the owned source is:

- `DEFAULT_CURSOR_TAIL` and `USAGE` at `src/main.rs:52-60`
- `LaunchArguments`, `launch_arguments`, `parse_cursor_color`, and `default_socket_path` at `src/main.rs:1541-1653` and `1674-1685`
- private `EON_VENUS_PRESENTATION_CONTROL=stdin` supervision selection currently at `src/main.rs:1531`
- the focused launch/default/error test at `src/main.rs:1734-1900`

The application receives one concrete validated launch value and does not reconstruct defaults or environment policy.

## Scope

In scope:
- move argument parsing, validation, usage text, cursor default/color parsing, default Orbit socket selection, and supervision selection to `launch.rs`
- move the directly coupled launch test with that owner
- expose only one crate-internal concrete launch value needed by the application
- keep the existing standard-library implementation

Out of scope:
- stdin presentation-control reading, control bytes, threads, `UserEvent`, event-loop construction, and native startup error projection; these remain for `ven-12v.2`
- changing flags, values, defaults, environment semantics, socket rules, colors, messages, ordering, or exit statuses
- deleting unrelated compile-dead code during the move
- a CLI framework, getters/builders, generic configuration layer, public API, dependency, or Eon/Orbit edit

## Ownership decision

Launch owns whether supervised mode is selected; application owns how the selected mode starts and routes the private control stream. This keeps `launch.rs` independent of winit and avoids a duplicate presentation-command type.

## Acceptance criteria

- `launch.rs` is the sole owner of CLI/default/environment launch policy and returns one validated crate-internal value.
- The application consumes that value directly without copying validation or defaults.
- Exact command syntax, invalid-input text, default socket, cursor profile, opacity, blur, decoration, supervision selection, error order, and exit behavior are unchanged.
- `main.rs` no longer contains launch parsing or launch constants; the application and presentation-control mechanics otherwise remain unchanged for the next child.
- No new dependency, public surface, protocol, platform conditional, or behavior is introduced.
- A proof-bearing source commit and follow-up metadata preserve or advance every touched contract as required.

## Reference gate and verification

Required before code: current `AGENTS.md`, this issue and parent, VEN-C1/C9/C11/C14/C15/C16, current launch source/tests, and the exact accepted ORBS/EONW revisions above. Monstar is not relevant to this parser move and remains comparison-only. No external crate or reference implementation is selected.

Use the existing focused launch test first, then one complete locked format/check/test/Clippy run for the unchanged candidate and `git diff --check`. Reuse accepted native proof because this child moves deterministic startup policy without changing it; the final application child owns bounded native Wayland and absent-Wayland observations. README LOC and contract metadata must be exact.

## Stop conditions

Stop if extraction changes any observable launch behavior, requires application or winit types in `launch.rs`, duplicates a default, needs a dependency/public surface, or cannot remain a direct move.
notes: Accepted source: bab89d1a31bdb7a6a5985f12443f1ace3b0d7f18. Binary-private src/launch.rs owns usage/defaults, CLI validation, cursor color/default, Orbit socket fallback, and exact private supervision selection. Application consumes one validated LaunchArguments and retains native window creation, event loop, control-stream mechanics, and error projection. Focused launch plus consuming checks pass; complete locked proof passes 59 library, 27 host, and 14 canonical integration tests with format/check/Clippy/diff clean. Rejected CLI dependency, getters/builders, public API, application/winit coupling in launch, duplicate defaults, protocol/platform/behavior changes, and unrelated cleanup. Accepted native proofs are reused because the deterministic values and native projection are unchanged.
close_reason: Launch policy is solely owned by src/launch.rs at source bab89d1a31bdb7a6a5985f12443f1ace3b0d7f18; exact launch behavior and all routed contracts are preserved by focused and complete locked proof.

title: Reduce Venus sustained complete-frame CPU below the acceptance ceiling
description:
## Why

Orbit acceptance Bead orb-bi4.5.4 found one confirmed pre-graduation no-go at Orbit 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564 and Venus 8149002c7275a00db1c08fded171e09f249dd977. Release builds at a 929x976 window and authoritative 100x52 grid ran timeout 20s sh -c "while :; do seq 1 20000; done". Combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 was 240 percent, above the predeclared 200 percent ceiling. A same-shape attribution sample measured Orbit p95 101 percent and Venus p95 141 percent, making Venus the larger process-level cost. RSS and final convergence passed: 8.2 MiB growth and 116 ms after output quiesced.

Effort: M. Risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH that Venus owns the larger observed share; the internal limiting stage is not yet identified.

## Evidence

- src/model.rs:141-144 materializes every accepted protocol frame into a fresh Scene.
- src/scene.rs:104-146 clones the complete frame into Venus draw rows and cells.
- src/main.rs:113-170 applies every server message, refreshes accessibility and window state, and requests redraw.
- src/render.rs:302-408 prepares text, records a complete render pass, submits, and presents.
- src/render.rs:411-434 rebuilds all scene text and rectangles whenever the revision changes.
- orb-bi4.5.4 records exact revisions, environment, ceilings, workload, and process-level measurements.

## Scope

In scope:
- Venus-owned complete-frame materialization, scene rebuild, glyph preparation, and presentation costs.
- Private, bounded profiling sufficient to identify the dominant Venus stage.
- The smallest Venus-only correction that brings the accepted complete-frame path below the existing envelope.
- Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and canonical ORBS v1.

Out of scope:
- Orbit code, tests, manifests, or ownership.
- A protocol revision, delta schema, dirty-row extraction, snapshot-plus-row-patch, public trace, alternate backend, or second terminal authority.
- History, ordered effects, graphics-resource expansion, remote transport, macOS support, or persistence.
- A direct crate unless a repository Crate gate selects it.

## Implementation Notes

1. Reproduce the exact release workload and segment Venus CPU among Scene::from_frame, refresh and accessibility, rebuild_if_needed, glyph preparation, submission, and presentation without changing the public boundary.
2. Identify the dominant measured stage before choosing code shape.
3. Apply the smallest Venus-owned correction and retain complete canonical frames plus snapshots as the resynchronization fallback.
4. Rerun the exact envelope and every canonical proof check for contracts touched.
5. If the measured cause requires an Orbit or protocol change, stop and report the compatibility decision instead of adding an adapter.

## Verification

- cargo fmt --check should exit 0.
- cargo check --locked should exit 0.
- cargo test --locked should exit 0.
- cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings should exit 0.
- The orb-bi4.5.4 sustained-output condition should report combined CPU p95 <= 200 percent, RSS <= 192 MiB, RSS growth <= 32 MiB, and final convergence <= 1 second.
- Shell, Neovim, Yazi, resize, and reattachment observations should preserve their accepted results.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop if the complete-frame flow has drifted materially from the cited revision.
- Stop if a correction requires changing ORBS v1, Orbit ownership, or another repository.
- Stop before adding a dependency, public instrumentation surface, dirty-row extraction, or patch protocol without the required gate and explicit user choice.
- Stop if the exact workload cannot reproduce the result; record the negative result rather than optimizing a guess.

## Maintenance Notes

This Bead hardens VEN-C1 and must preserve VEN-C2, VEN-C3, and VEN-C4. It consumes compatible ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 proofs through Orbit 847cab1. Complete frames remain accepted unless measured evidence and a separate user decision change the boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The exact orb-bi4.5.4 release workload is reproducible and attributes the dominant Venus CPU stage with observed data.
2. A Venus-only correction brings combined Orbit plus Venus CPU p95 to <= 200 percent at 929x976 and 100x52 while RSS remains <= 192 MiB, growth <= 32 MiB, and final convergence <= 1 second.
3. VEN-C1 is hardened and VEN-C2 through VEN-C4 remain behaviorally preserved; canonical checks pass on the resulting exact revision.
4. ORBS v1, complete canonical frames, snapshot resynchronization, Orbit ownership, and the one-client boundary do not change.
5. No direct crate, public trace, dirty-row extraction, snapshot-plus-row-patch, adapter, or cross-repository change is introduced without its required gate and explicit user choice.
notes: Accepted state: Venus source proof 8929c9f9d151641a343813ddeb6005cb9c771286 and proof metadata cea6b00e122968fa5bd3f92ffb6b9d8bf54c2b4c harden VEN-C1 and preserve VEN-C2 through VEN-C4 against Orbit runtime 847cab1ca37495c5cd45454623bd81909b488564 and unchanged canonical protocol c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6. Venus keeps one bounded native event queue. Complete frames are replaced across ordered Accepted acknowledgements only when the queued candidate is strictly newer than every previously delivered or queued frame and the incoming frame is strictly newer again; otherwise original order reaches FrameReducer, which remains the sole revision validator. Failures, invalid data, connection loss, and other semantic barriers retain ordering and first-cause behavior. ASCII uses basic shaping; non-ASCII retains advanced shaping. Exact Xwayland acceptance at 929x976 and 100x52 measured active combined CPU p95 167 percent, Orbit maximum 101 percent, Venus maximum 67 percent, peak combined RSS about 55.3 MiB, and 13.6 ms final convergence. Fifty fullscreen cycles returned coherently to 929x976 within 500 ms, and current state reattached in 122 ms while Orbit and its PTY survived client loss. Shell, Unicode, Neovim, and Yazi evidence remains preserved. Simplification retained one strong frame-reduction test for message barriers, delivered high-water, and non-increasing revisions. Container replacement, derived frame counting, notifier inlining, and batch refresh were rejected because they increased code or runtime work, moved rather than removed the concurrency concept, or risked observable accessibility/failure behavior. title: Provide native history scrolling, selection, and copy
description:
Contract routing:
- Creates VEN-C7 when implementation is explicitly activated.
- Consumes ORB-C8 at `840a67c0cb32b334ed54888321d5ca77e58117b0` and ORB-C9 plus the breaking ORBS v2 replacement at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Preserves VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and keeps Orbit as the sole terminal, retained-history, viewport, selection, selected-presentation, and copied-text authority.
- Planning this Bead changes no product contract, protocol, manifest, or runtime behavior.

Goal:
Prove the minimum useful native-terminal interaction in Venus against the exact accepted Orbit owner. Venus captures native gestures, maps them to the last accepted complete frame, presents Orbit-authored selection, and performs the explicit native clipboard side effect. It does not cache or reconstruct terminal history.

Accepted compatibility order:
1. Orbit has proved ORBS v2 and ORB-C9 at `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
2. After Orbit `orb-j0m.5` closes, activate this Bead as the next single implementation frontier.
3. Update the exact `orbit-protocol` pin from the ORBS v1 consumer revision `c905bf9610581747f1b07565814b501ca66cfaa6` to the accepted Orbit proof.
4. Prove Venus, then let Orbit `orb-j0m.4` accept the real pair.

This is a breaking owner-to-consumer update. There is no ORBS v1 adapter, dual-version support, feature probe, compatibility window, second decoder, or handwritten schema.

Implementation shape:
- Wheel and trackpad input use the existing canonical semantic mouse message. Venus owns only bounded native scroll normalization: line deltas accumulate in line units, while pixel deltas normalize against the current rendered cell dimensions, and either source emits only whole semantic wheel steps. It keeps at most a sub-step remainder, drops non-finite input, caps emissions per native event, and clears residual state on focus loss, scale or geometry change, and reconnect. Orbit alone resolves authoritative application mouse tracking, DEC 1007 alternate scroll, primary-history viewport movement, clamping, no-op framing, and byte-producing-key return to live.
- Pointer gestures are mapped against the last accepted complete-frame revision and current viewport cells. Venus sends canonical ORBS v2 Begin, Update, Finish, and Copy actions in order.
- Orbit-authored complete frames remain the only source of cells, selected styling, cursor, title, and reconnect state. Venus keeps only transient native gesture state and the accepted frame required to render and hit-test it.
- Orbit returns exact bounded CopiedText only after an explicit Copy action. Venus writes that result to the native clipboard and never extracts terminal text from rendered cells.
- A non-selection terminal mutation cancels active selection. After Finish, terminal output, resize or reflow, and active-screen transitions clear selected presentation without changing the frozen copy candidate. A newer valid Begin, client loss, or exit clears it.
- Accessibility derives viewport and selection from the same accepted complete frame and reports interaction failures without inventing missing terminal state.

Explicit non-owners:
Venus has no history page cache, epoch, stable row anchor, row token, page request, gap repair, cache eviction, client-owned viewport, client-owned terminal selection content, or text reconstruction. Search, semantic command regions, richer word/line/rectangle selection, drag autoscroll, auto-copy, rich clipboard formats, terminal clipboard-write effects, restart persistence, tabs, panes, and workspace topology remain outside this Bead.

References before code:
- Required: exact Orbit ORB-C8/ORB-C9 proof and canonical ORBS v2 package; current Venus Scene, renderer, input, accessibility, lifecycle, and failure owners; exact winit and AccessKit surfaces already selected by the repository; and the repository's native clipboard path or a triggered native-platform decision.
- Comparison only: one mature native terminal interaction at an exact revision, limited to gesture precedence, accessibility, and clipboard UX.
- Rejected scope: client-side VT parsing, page caches, stable anchors, replay protocols, copied terminal implementations, and compatibility adapters.

Cheapest proof:
Use deterministic protocol-faithful tests against the exact canonical Orbit package for scroll-delta normalization, gesture-to-cell mapping, action ordering, stale revision rejection, authoritative selected frames, frozen copy behavior, mouse-mode precedence, reconnect, and bounded failure. Then dogfood the real Linux Orbit/Venus pair through shell history, rapid wheel movement, key return to live, wrapped Unicode and wide graphemes, forward and reverse selection, explicit copy, resize/reflow, alternate-screen Neovim and Yazi, mouse mode, DEC 1007, detach, reattach, client loss, oversized copy, and stopped-reader pressure.

Acceptance:
1. VEN-C7 and the exact ORB-C8/ORB-C9 proof revisions are indexed before implementation; the manifest pins the accepted ORBS v2 `orbit-protocol` revision.
2. Native wheel and trackpad deltas become a bounded count of canonical semantic wheel steps: fractional line movement accumulates in line units, sub-cell pixel movement accumulates against current cell dimensions, emission is capped, and residual state resets at native lifecycle boundaries. The resulting steps traverse Orbit-owned retained history and return to live without client history state or duplicate PTY bytes.
3. Application mouse reporting and DEC 1007 behavior remain Orbit-owned and take correct precedence over host scrolling.
4. Selection begins only against the exact last accepted complete-frame revision; stale revisions, invalid cells, invalid phase order, oversized work, and pressure fail deterministically without partial client state.
5. Venus renders authoritative selected styling from complete frames and never reparses or mirrors terminal text.
6. Explicit Copy places only Orbit-returned bounded CopiedText on the native clipboard. Output, resize/reflow, and screen transitions preserve the finished frozen candidate exactly as ORB-C9 specifies.
7. Resize/reflow, alternate-screen transitions, mutation cancellation, detach/reattach, client loss, and reconnect converge without a cache, stable-anchor, or second terminal owner.
8. Accessibility exposes the same accepted viewport, selected styling, copy success or failure, and reconnect state used visually.
9. Deterministic checks and real Linux dogfood cover the stated boundary; canonical locked Rust checks and git diff checking pass.
10. Closure records exact Orbit and Venus revisions, VEN-C and ORB-C IDs, breaking update order, commands, environment, bounds, latency, memory, queued output, dependency disposition, portability, LOC, and remaining limitations.
11. Orbit `orb-j0m.4` can accept the exact real pair for Eon dogfood without an adapter or client-side compensation.

Dependency decision:
No dependency is selected. Reuse the accepted Venus stack and native platform facilities. Any new crate or architecture-shaping native choice requires the repository gate and user approval.

Portability disposition:
Neutral gesture and protocol flow with clipboard and window-system effects isolated at existing platform seams. Linux is the proof target; macOS remains credible but unproved.

External gate:
This is the sole Venus consumer Bead for the pre-graduation native-interaction baseline. Keep it deferred until Orbit `orb-j0m.5` closes, then activate it as the next single implementation frontier. Orbit `orb-j0m.4` and Eon dogfood wait for the accepted VEN-C7 proof.

This is the user-approved breaking owner-first ORBS v2 replacement recorded by ven-4sn, adds no second package or adapter, removes no project-owned LOC, and requires the exhaustive consumer update for Selection and CopiedText. The exact scratch cargo check failed at dependency fetch with revision not found. The remote commit must be published before a locked Venus proof can exist; no local-path or compatibility substitute is accepted.

Native clipboard candidates:

1. Standard library, winit 0.30.13, and existing dependency graph: rejected because none owns a native clipboard write. External wl-copy, xclip, or xsel commands are rejected as undeclared runtime and process-lifetime dependencies with inconsistent X11, Wayland, Nix, and macOS behavior. Handwritten X11, Wayland, and AppKit integration is rejected because it would add unsafe and substantial platform ownership beneath a forbid-unsafe crate for one bounded text operation.

2. arboard 3.6.1, exact crates.io release, MIT OR Apache-2.0, recommended with default features disabled and wayland-data-control enabled. It owns set_text, X11 fallback, Wayland data-control, macOS AppKit, clipboard hosting, and typed failure. A scratch locked cargo check passed with the existing Venus stack. The all-target lock adds 12 packages: arboard 3.6.1, wl-clipboard-rs 0.9.3, os_pipe 1.2.3, tree_magic_mini 3.2.2, nom 8.0.0, petgraph 0.8.3, fixedbitset 0.5.7, hashbrown 0.15.5, foldhash 0.1.5, clipboard-win 5.4.1, error-code 3.3.2, and objc2-app-kit 0.3.2. Expected Venus-owned cost is one retained Clipboard field and one bounded write/error path, about 15 to 25 handwritten lines; exact LOC will be recorded after implementation. Upgrade burden is one direct version and feature selection. Removal or replacement is isolated to that field and write path.

Linux behavior: arboard first attempts the optional Wayland data-control protocol and falls back to X11. This covers the accepted Linux/Xwayland slice and wlroots-style data-control compositors; native Wayland environments without data-control and without Xwayland may reject initialization and remain an explicit unproved platform gap. macOS feasibility is credible through its native AppKit backend but remains unproved. Input and accessibility ownership are unchanged; success and failure are exposed through the existing Venus status and AccessKit alert path. A future browser client would replace this isolated native effect with the browser clipboard API rather than carry arboard across the boundary.

3. copypasta 0.10.2, exact crates.io release, MIT OR Apache-2.0: rejected. Its generic Unix ClipboardContext is X11-only; correct Wayland use requires selecting a separate provider from a raw display pointer through an unsafe constructor, which conflicts with the repository forbid-unsafe boundary and adds Venus-owned runtime dispatch. Alacritty uses that larger integration because it already owns those platform handles; Venus does not.

Security, data, and proof: pass at most the canonical 1 MiB ORBS v2 CopiedText directly to set_text, enable no reads or image formats, retain no second text copy, and surface initialization or write failure. First crate check after approval is locked compile against the published 9d6d2bb pin; focused model and clipboard-side-effect checks follow. title: Make Eon workspace navigation direct and pane headers visible
description:
## Contract routing

Change and harden VEN-C8 under the user-approved 2026-08-09 contract. In Eon workspace mode, Alt+H/L selects the previous/next tab, Alt+K/J selects the previous/next pane, Alt+M creates one pane, and Ctrl+T creates one tab through existing EONW semantic actions. Creation ignores key repeat; direct traversal may repeat. Standalone Venus passes these keys to Orbit unchanged. F6/arrow/Escape focus navigation remains available.

Every pane in the active tab has one visible ordered header whenever the headers plus a useful terminal body fit. Exactly the selected pane exposes its terminal body immediately after its header. When they do not fit, bounded pane scrolling preserves the existing overflow mechanism and reveals the selected pane without hiding otherwise fitting siblings.

Important failures: unavailable workspace transport reports the existing bounded failure and preserves accepted state; rejected Eon actions preserve the accepted scene; tiny windows remain bounded; no shortcut creates duplicate requests from key repeat.

Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 and VEN-C7, Orbit ownership, Eon topology/action ownership, the exact EONW schema, accessibility order/actions, pointer behavior, and one expanded terminal. No new dependency, protocol, configuration surface, split model, or module.

## Evidence and references

Required before code: AGENTS.md, this Bead, VEN-C8 and its proof, current workspace scene/render/input/application owners and tests, exact Eon/EONW producer proof 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d, exact Orbit/ORBS proof 9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757, and the user-named Nova project at an exact commit for shortcut behavior only. Existing Canario/Rio 3e41b8b19a1cad9cd9bdfc8f7900cf61ce5a9098 remains comparison-only for accordion geometry. Reuse no reference source.

## Acceptance

A deterministic failing-then-passing check proves all four direct directions, the two creation actions, modifier gating, creation repeat suppression, standalone passthrough, and retained F6 navigation. Accordion checks prove two and three pane headers are simultaneously visible around the selected expanded body at ordinary sizes, selected-body adjacency, bounded tiny/overflow geometry, hit testing, and stable order. Accessibility derives the same order. Locked Rust format, check, tests, clippy, git diff check, and focused native Linux dogfood pass. README, CHANGELOG, contract proof state, agent policy if affected, and LOC are accurate. No commit, push, Eon pin, runtime replacement, or distribution is included without separate user direction.

title: Accept Orbit continuous-output scrollback in Venus
description:
## Outcome and contract routing

Consumer: one Venus terminal user, including a Venus surface launched by Eon.

Trigger: Orbit publishes an accepted exact ORB-C8 proof for orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi, and Venus previews or commits retained-history movement while terminal output continues to advance frames.

Result: Venus consumes that exact compatible Orbit revision and preserves its existing fractional, kinetic, wheel, selection, and rendering behavior while the user can enter and continue scrollback during continuous TUI output. The stale preview/scroll notices from the dogfood report do not appear, the gesture is not starved, and an entered viewport remains pinned as output continues.

This hardens VEN-C7 and consumes the new exact ORB-C8 proof. Preserve every other VEN-C contract. If Orbit changes ORBS bytes or version, stop before consumer edits and require an explicitly approved breaking rollout; this Bead assumes unchanged ORBS v10.

## Ownership and sequencing

Orbit remains the sole terminal, history, viewport, routing, revision, and PTY owner. Venus owns native input accumulation, one in-flight scroll batch, fractional/kinetic presentation, rendering, and truthful notices. Venus must not compensate with failure-detail string matching, a blind retry loop, cached history, or a second revision policy.

Sequence:
1. orb-keep-scrollback-usable-during-output-rgi proves the producer and records the exact compatible revision.
2. This Bead pins that revision, proves the current Venus interaction path against it, and publishes one exact consumer revision.
3. Eon adoption `eon-adopt-continuous-output-scrollback-umf` selects the accepted Orbit/Venus pair and refreshes the installed profile.

Status is deferred until the Orbit proof exists. Native Linux Wayland remains the only product surface.

## Evidence

Current application.rs sends PreviewVertical and ScrollVertical from the last presented revision, allows one batch in flight, exposes Orbit InvalidInput through the model, and resets terminal scrolling after a server failure. Current VEN-C7 treats stale presentation as a cancellation. The Orbit defect makes that valid client behavior user-visible under continuous output.

The Orbit lifecycle proof already establishes that a successfully entered authoritative viewport stays pinned across later PTY output. This consumer slice should need no new terminal or freeze state.

## Scope boundary

In scope: exact Orbit source/protocol pin, VEN-C7 contract/proof refresh, focused model/application/transport coverage needed for the compatible producer, native dogfood, documentation, changelog after acceptance, and LOC accounting.

Out of scope: Eon component/profile updates, client-owned history, generic retry, string matching on failure details, a new protocol version, gesture redesign, public tuning, new renderer/input module, dependencies, or platform expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance_criteria field is authoritative. Venus must accept the exact compatible Orbit proof, retain its existing scroll/input/render owners, pass focused and native continuous-output checks, and publish one exact consumer revision without a retry workaround.

title: Accept Venus on Apple Silicon with Orbit
description:
## Outcome and contract

Accept the complete native Venus Apple Silicon slice against exact Orbit authority and hand a proof-bearing Venus revision to Eon composition.

- Consumer: standalone Venus diagnostics and the existing Eon Apple Silicon composition epic.
- Trigger: launch the final aarch64-darwin Venus candidate against accepted native Orbit, and exercise its workspace client with the exact accepted Eon workspace protocol.
- Result: one native Venus process renders and controls the authoritative Orbit Session through the shared model/scene/renderer/action path, preserves workspace and popup behavior through an exact protocol substitute, survives reconnect and owned failures, and leaves a complete VEN-C16 proof record for Eon to consume.
- Important failures: identity mismatch, attach/reconnect loss, stale frames, Orbit exit, Venus exit, invalid workspace state, renderer recovery, clipboard/input/accessibility/presentation regression, or missing proof fails explicitly without moving PTY, workspace, lifecycle, or composition ownership into Venus.

This is the final Venus acceptance child. It may mark the Apple Silicon portion of VEN-C16 Proven only after the preceding four children and this exact native dogfood are accepted. It changes no Eon contract and does not prove full Eon on macOS.

## Ownership and sequencing

Require accepted opaque host, interaction/pasteboard, accessibility/lifecycle/identity, and Metal transparency/blur children at exact revisions. Consume Orbit ORB-C14 from accepted source 0233f4d34b294a50c5bc7f373859cf4ec04d2414 and the exact current ORBF v2 / ORBS v11 package revision selected at implementation baseline. Orbit owns PTY, Session, terminal state, copied text, and attachment. Venus owns native presentation and semantic interaction. Eon owns component graph, Nix composition, managed tools, launch/update policy, and full-product dogfood.

Use exact Eon workspace protocol fixtures or a bounded substitute to prove Venus-owned tabs, panes, shared popups, shortcut viewer, picker projection, failure handling, and caller inputs. Do not require an unproved full Eon macOS build before Venus can close; that would create a cycle. After acceptance, update the external handoff to eon-prove-full-eon-apple-silicon-macos-t8o, which owns Nix packaging and complete product proof.

## Reference gate

Read this bead and parent, every preceding child and accepted proof, complete current VEN-C1 through VEN-C20 index and touched checks, accepted ORB-C14 contracts/proof and exact current protocol source, exact Eon workspace protocol/fixtures, current Venus transport/model/application/render/accessibility/launch owners, and relevant docs/REFERENCES.md and docs/CRATES.md routes. Inspect official macOS behavior only for a concrete unresolved native failure from the dogfood. Reuse exact preceding reference decisions; do not repeat them or widen claims. Record exact candidate identities, dirty state, preserved contracts, unresolved limitations, and first outermost check.

## Scope and verification

In scope: exact native Orbit launch/attach/reconnect/loss; authoritative rendering, input, resize, selection/copy/paste, links, accessibility, tabs/panes/popups, shortcut viewer, configured presentation, surface recovery, Venus close/quit with Orbit survival, workspace-protocol failure UX, Linux regression proof, VEN-C16 evidence/status, changelog and LOC, and the Eon handoff identity.

Out of scope: modifying Eon composition or Orbit behavior; Nix package graph; Helix/Yazi/Ratconfig availability; installer, signing, notarization, Homebrew, direct bundles, public release, Intel macOS, remote transport, another protocol, compatibility window, or broader platform support.

Cheapest proof:

2. On real Apple Silicon, exercise one retained Orbit Session through launch, authoritative Unicode output, keyboard/IME/pointer/trackpad, resize/scale, history selection and copy/paste, link Open/Copy, accessibility actions, opacity values and truthful blur behavior, surface recovery, detach/reconnect, Orbit loss, Venus close/quit, and reattachment.
3. Exercise exact workspace protocol state for tabs, panes, shared popups, shortcut viewer, picker projection, caller identity, malformed/lost workspace input, and recovery without claiming Eon composition.
4. Record exact source, Orbit/protocol revisions, hardware, macOS/Rust identities, commands, artifacts, observations, failures, limits, dependency/LOC delta, proof phase, and Eon handoff. Update docs/CONTRACTS.md only from the accepted proof-bearing source commit.

If native acceptance needs unavailable interactive hardware, user action, a change in Orbit/Eon ownership, Nix composition, or a new dependency, stop and ask the user. Do not substitute compilation, an opaque screenshot, or full-Eon assumptions for this proof.

title: Admit published AccessKit workspace actions
description:
## Contract

Preserve VEN-C8. When assistive technology invokes Click or Focus on a tab or pane node from the latest AccessKit tree Venus has published, Venus queues exactly one matching EONW v1 FocusId without waiting for GPU presentation. Venus changes its local focus region only after that action enters the bounded Eon workspace queue. Pointer, keyboard, and terminal input remain admitted only against the matching GPU-presented composite. Unsupported or retired accessibility nodes remain no-ops, and queue failure keeps the existing bounded visible workspace-loss path.

## Evidence

The completed integration audit `ven-audit-venus-integration-mtj` records F1 on Venus `81fabbacf9199f16b665b3b9bedf471e7f75eeca`: `docs/CRATES.md:141-147` requires accepted-scene accessibility publication during GPU occlusion or recovery, while `src/main.rs:501-506,1228-1256` routes those published actions through the GPU gate and changes local focus before queue admission. Presented mouse activation has the same focus-before-queue failure ordering.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

Consume unchanged EONW v1 producer `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`, Orbit protocol proof `7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c`, AccessKit 0.24.1, accesskit_winit 0.33.2, `docs/REFERENCES.md` native-workspace and selected-crate entries, `docs/CRATES.md` selected owner seam, and VEN-C8. AccessKit and EONW are required exact owner evidence; renderer references are comparison only because their mechanism does not change. Add no dependency, schema, protocol, module, or compatibility path.

## Scope

In scope: the Application-owned admission and focus ordering for current AccessKit tab and pane actions; preserving presented-composite admission for visual and keyboard input; one focused deterministic regression; current documentation and LOC metadata required by repository policy.

Out of scope: new accessibility actions, announcements, stale-node compatibility, protocol changes, renderer changes, macOS or compositor expansion, and native GUI dogfood that would change desktop focus.

## Acceptance

- An action for a current published AccessKit tab or pane queues one exact EONW FocusId while GPU presentation is invalid.
- Local workspace focus changes if and only if the FocusId enters the bounded Eon queue.
- Retired or unknown nodes remain inert.
- Pointer and keyboard workspace actions remain blocked until their composite is successfully presented.
- Existing queue-failure diagnostics, transport bounds, stable AccessKit identities, and terminal focus generation semantics remain intact.
- Locked formatting, checks, tests, Clippy, diff checks, LOC scorecard, and Beads lint pass.

title: Adopt canonical Orbit cell-width validation
description:
## Contract routing

Consumer-side adoption after Orbit issue `orb-validate-orbf-cell-width-topology-qcs`. Hardens existing `VEN-C1` and `VEN-C4` and preserves `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C3`, `VEN-C7`, `VEN-C8`, `VEN-C10`, and `VEN-C13`; it adds or changes no product contract. Venus continues to consume one exact canonical `orbit-protocol` revision and adds no validator, schema, or compatibility window.

Deferred until:
1. `orb-validate-orbf-cell-width-topology-qcs` closes with an accepted immutable compatible-hardening proof;
2. the current cross-repository implementation frontier is handed back for consumer adoption.

Current Venus pin is `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174`. Record the eventual accepted Orbit proof and every affected `ORB-C*` revision before claiming.

## Why

Consumer: Venus Scene materialization and every native presentation built from canonical ORBF v1 frames.

Trigger: Orbit publishes the accepted canonical package revision that rejects producer-invalid Wide/SpacerTail/SpacerHead topology.

Result: Venus pins exactly that accepted package, consumes the canonical rejection without duplicating it, proves its valid wide and wrapped-cell fixtures, and preserves bounded invalid-frame UX.

Important failures: do not compensate in `Scene`, keep the old vulnerable pin, accept two protocol revisions, or advance the dependency without exact Orbit proof and compatibility classification.

Audit `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db` found that `Scene::build_glyph_runs` correctly relies on a validated frame but the current canonical package does not own the required topology. Orbit issue `orb-validate-orbf-cell-width-topology-qcs` owns the upstream correction. Impact MED. Effort S. Implementation risk MED because an exact direct dependency and proof metadata advance. Confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `Cargo.toml:13` and `Cargo.lock:1683-1685`: Venus pins exact Orbit `3ee7c800...`.
- `README.md:28-29,123`, `docs/REFERENCES.md:11,133`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md:16,23-24`, and `docs/CRATES.md:14`: canonical documentation names the same exact accepted package.
- `src/scene.rs:435-535`: Scene documents a validated-frame precondition and interprets Wide as a two-column head while skipping SpacerHead/SpacerTail roles.
- `tests/canonical_scene.rs:523-566`: the canonical Venus fixture uses a valid same-row Wide plus SpacerTail and proves deterministic projection.
- Orbit issue `orb-validate-orbf-cell-width-topology-qcs` records current validator evidence, exact selected libghostty topology sources, compatibility gate, and owner-first implementation proof requirements.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. At the current Venus pin, encode/decode a canonical frame with adjacent Wide cells, missing SpacerTail, or orphan SpacerTail; the canonical package accepts it.
2. Feed the decoded frame through `SessionModel`/Scene; observe that wide-column skipping can omit cells or make run arithmetic invalid.
3. After the exact accepted Orbit hardening exists, update only the dependency pin and repeat the same canonical decode; expected rejection occurs before Scene.
4. Confirm all valid Venus canonical wide/wrapped fixtures continue to decode and materialize identically.

## Scope

In scope:
- `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` exact `orbit-protocol` proof revision.
- Canonical Venus fixtures/tests only where the accepted validator proves an existing fixture invalid.
- Existing model/Scene invalid-frame failure checks and the narrowest canonical valid-wide/wrapped consumer proof.
- `README.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, `docs/CRATES.md`, and `docs/CONTRACTS.md` exact producer/consumer proof metadata.
- README LOC scorecard if tracked handwritten Rust changes; CHANGELOG only if accepted consumer-visible protocol compatibility behavior warrants it.

Out of scope:
- Any Orbit edit; a Venus width validator; Scene repair/normalization; schema mirror; second protocol revision; compatibility adapter/window; renderer redesign; new dependency; or changes to Orbit-owned width semantics.

## Reference and crate gate

Required before code:
- This complete Bead, `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db`, and the complete closed Orbit issue `orb-validate-orbf-cell-width-topology-qcs` with its accepted source/proof commits.
- Current `AGENTS.md`, `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact accepted Orbit canonical package source, width-topology tests, compatibility classification, `ORB-C4`/`ORB-C6` proof rows, and all other changed package behavior since `3ee7c800...`.
- Current Venus protocol import, decoder/reducer/model/Scene paths, canonical fixtures, and invalid-frame UX.

Comparison-only: no external terminal or renderer is needed; Orbit's selected libghostty evidence owns the topology.

Rejected: consumer validation, normalization, compatibility path, another schema, or dependency.

Crate gate: required before manifest edits because this advances an exact direct architecture-shaping dependency. Record exact old/new commits; product LOC effect; unchanged direct/transitive/native/build/Nix footprint; upgrade burden; Linux/macOS/browser implications; relied-on focused behavior; compatibility classification; and replacement cost. Stop for user approval before editing `Cargo.toml`.

Platform disposition: neutral. Validation is platform-independent; Linux remains the runtime proof target and macOS remains unproved.

## Implementation notes

1. Reconfirm both Orbit prerequisites are accepted and published; do not build against an uncommitted or moving candidate.
2. Record Execution baseline and Reference gate, then the direct-dependency Crate gate and obtain user approval before manifest edits.
3. Use TDD/contract-first proof: demonstrate current pin accepts the malformed canonical frame and the accepted new pin rejects it before Scene; keep only the permanent post-adoption check that protects the boundary without duplicating Orbit internals.
4. Advance the exact Git pin with no compatibility adapter.
5. Correct only Venus fixtures shown invalid by the accepted producer contract; valid Scene behavior must remain identical.
6. Run complete locked checks, commit source/manifest consumer candidate first, then update exact proof metadata and close in the follow-up commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Venus pins the exact published Orbit proof that canonically rejects invalid cell-width topology.
- Malformed width roles fail in the canonical decoder/reducer and reach existing bounded invalid-frame UX; `Scene` adds no compensating check.
- Valid same-row wide pairs and accepted wrapped SpacerHead sequences materialize deterministically without visual/input regression.
- All other canonical ORBS v3 messages and VEN-C2/C3/C7/C10/C13 behavior remain preserved.
- Docs and crate decision name one exact Orbit proof and no stale `3ee7c800...` current-pin claim remains.
- Direct/transitive/native/build/Nix dependency footprint is unchanged except the exact source revision.
- No compatibility window, second schema, dependency, or product contract is introduced.

## Verification

- Focused current-pin/new-pin boundary falsifier as recorded at the Reference gate.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- `br lint <this-id>`

All commands must exit 0 on one materially unchanged source/manifest candidate; record test counts and exact environment. Native visual proof is required only if a valid fixture or rendering output changes; otherwise retain the existing visual proofs without widening them.

## Stop conditions

- Stop until the exact Orbit owner proof is accepted and published.
- Stop if Orbit classifies the hardening as breaking or requires a new ORBF/ORBS revision; ask the user to choose update order and compatibility.
- Stop if the new package contains unrelated behavior that cannot be adopted under this contract routing.
- Stop before a manifest edit without the Crate gate and explicit user approval.
- Stop before a Venus validator, schema mirror, adapter, new dependency, product contract change, or cross-repository edit.
- Stop if another active issue owns the protocol import, Scene, model, or canonical fixtures.

## Maintenance notes

Orbit owns canonical topology; Venus owns only exact-revision consumption and deterministic materialization. The removal path is the dependency pin—there must be no local validation layer to remove later.

title: Align AccessKit geometry with the rendered workspace
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens proved VEN-C2 shared geometry coherence and VEN-C8 accessible workspace materialization while preserving VEN-C1, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, status/activation behavior, EONW v1, and ORBS v4. It adds or changes no product contract, dependency, workspace topology, or screen-reader compatibility promise.

Consumes unchanged Eon EON-C10/EONW v1 at exact proof 4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d and Orbit ORBS v4 at exact proof 7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c.

The prior Eon terminal-child refresh frontier is closed. The user activated this issue as the sole active cross-repository implementation frontier.

## Why

Consumers: assistive technologies using AccessKit bounds for spatial navigation, touch exploration, caret tracking, or highlight placement.

Trigger: Venus publishes terminal TextRun geometry or a scrolled Eon tab/pane workspace.

Result: accessibility uses the exact current CellMetrics, terminal origin, padding, row/column counts, and workspace viewport clipping already used by drawing and native hit testing. Raw layout coordinates may remain for stable composition, but clipped descendants cannot appear spatially outside their visible parent regions.

Important failures: do not create a second metric owner, stretch rows to fill leftover surface pixels, flatten scrollable topology, hide legitimately navigable offscreen identities, or claim optional per-character geometry that is not implemented.

Audit ven-audit-venus-accessibility-p2h found two manifestations of this one spatial-projection owner at Venus 4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8. Impact MED. Effort S/M. Implementation risk LOW/MED. Confidence HIGH in the structural mismatch.

## Evidence

- docs/CONTRACTS.md:9 says one shared scaled metric owner keeps accessibility coherent with the 10×18 grid and proves 93×32 cells on 960×600.
- src/main.rs:518-558 passes renderer size but not CellMetrics or scene dimensions into Accessibility.
- src/accessibility.rs:310-321 divides the outer terminal rectangle evenly by row count and starts at its outer origin.
- src/render.rs:92-101 defines the 1× 10×18 grid with 12 px padding; src/render.rs:731-756 draws row r at terminal top + padding + r × cell height.
- src/main.rs:1229-1247 derives terminal rows only after removing the shared padding.
- src/scene.rs:228-255 intersects tabs, panes, and terminal geometry with workspace viewports for native hit testing.
- src/render.rs:598-655 intersects and clips tab/pane drawing; terminal drawing uses visible_terminal and the same clip owner.
- src/accessibility.rs:71-130 publishes raw child bounds but does not set clips_children on TAB_LIST, PANE_PANEL, or CONTENT.
- src/accessibility.rs:434-516 currently expects one TextRun to fill the complete raw terminal layout rectangle.
- AccessKit 0.24.1 src/lib.rs:1798-1820 defines ClipsChildren for exactly this relationship; lines 2152-2177 define physical window-relative bounds.
- Exact selected accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 `filters.rs:65-88` uses `clips_children` to filter fully offscreen subtrees while deliberately retaining an adjacent offscreen sibling; `node.rs:305-377` reports and hit-tests each node's own transformed bounds without intersecting ancestor clips. Exact accesskit_atspi_common 0.19.1 `node.rs:509-531,1047-1084` likewise returns those un-intersected bounds for AT-SPI extents, contains, and point lookup. The flag alone therefore does not prove partial-bound clipping on the selected Linux adapter.
- Audit comment 316 records the exact 960×600 drift calculation and scrolled-workspace mismatch; duplicate search found no existing owner.

## Scope

In scope:
- src/accessibility.rs Snapshot inputs, TextRun bounds, workspace container clipping declarations, and focused geometry tests.
- src/main.rs refresh/error call sites only to pass the existing renderer metrics and current Scene dimensions.
- Existing CellMetrics and WorkspaceScene values as read-only owners; change them only if a focused test proves their current public seam cannot supply the accepted geometry.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md VEN-C2/VEN-C8 proof metadata after a proof-bearing source commit, README LOC accounting, and CHANGELOG for the accepted correction.

Out of scope:
- New geometry types or modules, renderer layout changes, terminal resize policy, workspace scrolling policy, tab/pane topology, NodeId identity, grapheme character units, character_positions/character_widths, bidi, screen-reader-specific workarounds, dependency changes, or macOS proof.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code:
- Current AGENTS.md, this Bead, audit ven-audit-venus-accessibility-p2h, VEN-C2/VEN-C8, docs/REFERENCES.md, and docs/CRATES.md.
- Current CellMetrics, surface_size, workspace layout/hit testing, renderer clipping, Accessibility tree/update, and related tests.
- Exact AccessKit 0.24.1 bounds, transforms, ClipsChildren, and text-run coordinate semantics; selected accesskit_consumer 0.38.0 filtering/hit-testing; and selected accesskit_atspi_common 0.19.1 extents/contains/point behavior.
- Exact EONW producer proof only to preserve ordered topology and selected pane geometry.

Comparison-only: no external terminal implementation is needed; current drawing/hit-test owners and selected AccessKit semantics define the result.

Rejected:
- A second accessibility grid, dividing leftover pixels across rows, clipping each child by rewriting topology, hiding offscreen nodes, adding character geometry, or adding a dependency.

Platform disposition: neutral physical geometry over the selected adapter. Linux is the proof target; macOS remains unproved.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build the current accessibility snapshot for a 960×600, 1×, 93×32 Scene. Rendering places row 0 at y=12..30 and row 31 at y=570..588, while the current TextRun projection divides the complete outer bounds into equal rows.
2. Build a workspace with a partially and fully scrolled tab, pane, and selected terminal. The current tree publishes their raw rectangles outside `tab_viewport`, `pane_viewport`, and `visible_terminal` and sets no clipping flags.
3. Against exact selected accesskit_consumer/accesskit_atspi_common, observe that `clips_children` alone does not intersect a retained child's partial extents or point hit region. The candidate must publish the existing Scene intersections (or no bounds when empty) while retaining tree identity, order, actions, focus state, and text.

## Acceptance Criteria

The canonical verifiable criteria are stored in this Bead's `acceptance_criteria` field.

## Implementation notes

1. Use TDD on the VEN-C2 oracle: at 960×600 and 1×, row 0 must be y=12..30 and row 31 y=570..588, not equal slices of the full window.
2. Flow the existing Renderer CellMetrics and accepted Scene row/column counts into the existing Accessibility snapshot. Do not recompute scale, padding, columns, or rows.
3. Derive each raw TextRun rectangle from terminal layout origin + padding + row × cell height, with horizontal extent bounded by accepted columns × cell width.
4. Set `CONTENT`, `TAB_LIST`, and `PANE_PANEL` to clip children, but do not treat that flag as geometric clipping. Reuse `SceneRect::intersection`: publish each tab and pane child's intersection with its existing viewport, and omit bounds when the intersection is empty while retaining the child identity, action, focus state, and order.
5. In a workspace, publish `CONTENT` only at `visible_terminal` and intersect each raw TextRun rectangle with that same visible terminal; omit a fully clipped row's bounds without removing its text or identity. Standalone TextRuns keep their exact rendered grid rectangles. Add no second clip type or topology rewrite.
6. Cover standalone and workspace geometry at 1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, and 2× plus partially visible tab, pane, and terminal regions.
7. Keep character_positions and character_widths absent in this slice; AccessKit documents them as optional and the audit retained them as a quality proof limit.
8. Run locked checks and focused Linux AT-SPI bounds/touch-exploration observation after deterministic values pass.
9. Follow the source-commit then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

Dependency decision: reuse existing CellMetrics, Scene/WorkspaceScene, and AccessKit. No crate or manifest edit is expected.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the accepted renderer and resize paths no longer share one CellMetrics owner.
- Stop if exact geometry requires changing Orbit dimensions, EONW topology, renderer layout, or workspace scrolling policy.
- Stop before a new module, dependency, transform framework, character-geometry promise, product contract, or platform workaround.
- Stop if another active issue owns CellMetrics, accessibility bounds, or workspace clipping.
- Stop and rebaseline if current source, exact producer proofs, or AccessKit version changes materially.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Standalone TextRun bounds equal the physical rendered grid rectangles from the existing CellMetrics, padding, terminal origin, and accepted Scene dimensions at all four proved scales.
2. The 960×600 1× oracle exposes 93×32 cells; row 0 is y=12..30 and row 31 is y=570..588, with no stretch into padding or leftover pixels.
3. Workspace tab, pane, CONTENT, and TextRun bounds equal the intersection of their existing raw Scene geometry with the applicable viewport or visible terminal. A fully clipped node retains identity, action, focus state, order, and text but publishes no bounds.
4. TAB_LIST, PANE_PANEL, and CONTENT also declare the exact child clipping already enforced by rendering and native hit testing; exact selected AccessKit consumer and AT-SPI checks prove no descendant extents, contains result, or point hit outside that visible intersection.
5. Scrolled or partially visible tabs and panes remain in Eon order and keyboard/accessibility navigation, but their spatial exposure cannot overlap visually different regions.
6. Resize, scale change, workspace scroll, activation, renderer failure, occlusion/recovery, focus, selection, and status alerts all publish geometry from the latest accepted snapshot without a second metric owner.
7. Focused deterministic tests cover standalone/workspace bounds, all proved scales, partial clipping, and unchanged order/focus.
8. An isolated Linux observation that does not take active-desktop focus records AccessKit/AT-SPI extents, contains, and point lookup after tab/pane scrolling and confirms no clipped target is exposed in another visual region; unsupported touch-exploration behavior remains explicit.
9. cargo fmt --check, cargo check --locked, cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings, and git diff --check all exit 0.
10. Closure records the proof-bearing Venus revision, exact producer/AccessKit identities, dependency disposition, portability, LOC, native proof, and optional character-geometry limit.
notes:
This consolidates audit findings F3 and F4 because both are one invariant: AccessKit physical geometry must consume the existing render/hit-test metric and clip owners. Splitting them would duplicate the same snapshot seam and proof corpus.

Priority P2. Cheapest falsifiers: the 960×600 row rectangles must match the visual grid, and a pane scrolled partly above pane_viewport must remain a tree child while its spatial extent is clipped by the panel.

title: Audit Venus accessibility projection
description:
## Contract routing

This is a read-only repository audit. It changes no VEN product contract, implements no feature or fix, and authorizes no dependency, compatibility surface, or public behavior. Audit one exact accepted revision and preserve all pre-existing worktree state.

## Why

Feature-local fresh-eyes and simplification passes can converge while assistive state can drift from the accepted scene, visible workspace order, focus, selection, status, or native activation lifecycle. This subsystem owns a distinct invariant and failure domain, so it needs one bounded whole-subsystem review that includes direct callers and consumers.

## Evidence

- `src/accessibility.rs:179`: Accessibility owns the latest native tree projection
- `src/accessibility.rs:206`: updates derive from accepted scene and workspace presentation inputs
- `src/scene.rs:537`: accessible content is derived from the same immutable Scene
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md:13`: VEN-C8 requires accessible topology order while VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 preserve terminal state

## Prerequisites and reference gate

- Complete every declared blocker and do not start while another issue or agent is changing an in-scope surface. Record the exact accepted Eon and Orbit producer revisions consumed by the audited snapshot.
- Route each rendering, interaction, accessibility, dependency, portability, or ownership question through `docs/REFERENCES.md`; read the applicable contract proofs, `docs/CRATES.md`, and exact producer or selected-crate sources for the question. Record exact identities, licenses where relevant, accepted mechanisms, rejected surrounding scope, ownership consequences, and the cheapest check in this Bead. Reuse prior evidence only when the question and exact revision still match.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/accessibility.rs`, scene accessibility derivation, application adapter calls, AccessKit activation/events, and related tests.
- Tree identity, roles, bounds, text runs, character lengths, selection positions, status alerts, workspace tab/pane order, focus, activation freshness, occlusion/recovery behavior, and lock failure handling.
- Existing VEN accessibility claims and the proved VEN-C8 workspace surface.
- Exclude general settings, screen-reader-specific compatibility promises, and terminal-content reconstruction.

Out of scope:
- Implementing, fixing, refactoring, or editing repository files.
- Adding or changing product contracts, dependencies, compatibility promises, or deferred features.
- Auditing behavior owned by another repository beyond verifying the consumed boundary.
- Creating remediation Beads unless the user separately authorizes a planning-only batch.

## Audit method

1. Record governing instructions, tracker state, accepted contract proofs, and immutable subject identity: clean HEAD, or HEAD plus a SHA-256 of the tracked binary diff and hashes of every in-scope untracked file. Preserve the exact dirty paths.
2. Read every in-scope owner, its direct callers and consumers, meaningful tests, contract rows, reference decisions, and dependency decisions.
3. Trace the observable flow end to end and audit correctness, failures, bounds, security boundaries, performance, tests, ownership, dependencies, portability, DX, and documentation.
4. Run a fresh-eyes correctness pass, then a separate simplification and ownership pass. Reject style preferences, speculative features, accepted tradeoffs, and duplicates of existing Beads.
5. Vet each remaining finding against exact file:line evidence and record impact, effort (S/M/L), implementation risk, confidence, the cheapest falsifying check, and why it merits action.
6. Repeat the complete review after any material planning correction or subject-snapshot change. Converge only when a final full pass over one unchanged recorded snapshot finds no additional actionable finding beyond the recorded set.
7. Record either the vetted findings or an explicit no-finding result in this Bead with the audited revision, commands, failures, and remaining proof limits.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The audit covers the complete stated subsystem and adjacent boundaries, not only recent diffs.
- Every finding is concrete, reproducible or directly evidenced, ownership-routed, and checked against existing Beads.
- No tracked project file or preserved untracked user artifact changes during the audit; generated build outputs do not alter the recorded subject snapshot.
- The final record identifies the exact subject snapshot; any in-scope subject change invalidates prior completion and requires a complete new pass.
- The final pass reports convergence under the declared lenses without widening that claim to runtime or platform behavior not exercised.
- Findings remain recommendations until the user chooses separate remediation work.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo check --locked` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo test --locked` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- `git diff --check` should exit 0 on the audited revision.
- A prior verification result may be cited instead of rerun only when its recorded subject snapshot, environment, command, and exercised surface match exactly; otherwise rerun it.
- `br sync --flush-only` should persist the audit record without changing implementation.
- Final status and diff inspection should show only the pre-existing worktree plus authorized Beads mutations.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if an active implementation owns or materially changes an in-scope surface.
- Stop if evidence requires a new contract, dependency decision, cross-repository owner change, or scope expansion.
- Stop and report rather than compensating for an upstream or downstream contract gap.
