title: Continue drag selection into older history with upward autoscroll
description:
## Outcome and contract

Extend the existing Orbit/Venus selection contract so a person can continue a drag selection into older retained history.

- Consumer: one person dragging a host-owned text selection in a Venus terminal surface.
- Trigger: the active left-button selection reaches the top visible terminal row and remains there while older primary-screen history exists.
- Result: selection continues upward at one bounded, usable cadence. Each accepted step moves Orbit's authoritative viewport toward older history and extends the same authoritative gesture through the newly visible top row. Releasing freezes and copies the exact complete selection through the existing clipboard contract. Reaching the oldest retained row stops movement without cancelling the selection.
- Important failures: terminal-routed mouse gestures, alternate-screen/no-history state, focus or pointer-capture loss, release, resize/reflow, attachment replacement, stale presentation, synchronized output, pressure, transport loss, and an exhausted history edge cannot create a second selection owner, leave scrolling running, invent rows, mix routes, lose release, or expose partial copied text.

This is a planning container. It proposes compatible extensions to VEN-C7 and Orbit ORB-C8/ORB-C9 through the next exact canonical ORBS revision; it changes no contract or runtime until its owner and consumer children are explicitly created and activated.

## Evidence

- `eon-desktop/src/application.rs:56-285,840-890`: Venus already has bounded authoritative preview/commit scrolling, one in-flight batch, edge detection, and an event-loop wakeup surface.
- `eon-desktop/src/application.rs:2293-2318`: native pointer motion already routes active selection updates through the current presented geometry, but no motion occurs when the pointer remains clamped at the top row.
- `eon-desktop/src/input.rs:338-380`: selection updates are suppressed when the bounded position has not changed, so a newly revealed top row cannot extend selection without an explicit owner-level transition.
- `eon-sessions/src/interaction.rs:307-365`: ordinary `ScrollVertical` unconditionally clears selection before moving the authoritative viewport.
- `eon-sessions/docs/CONTRACTS.md:266-312`: ORB-C8 promises that ordinary committed scrolling clears active selection.
- `eon-sessions/docs/CONTRACTS.md:326-389`: ORB-C9 makes Orbit the sole gesture, boundary, selected-presentation, and copied-text owner and explicitly excludes autoscroll.
- Current exact identities at discovery: Eon Desktop `43ea277d50f7f06e9ca6a5c38e8d9a09bbe6ea84`; Eon Sessions `aee15e0006086952feaca28f95bd28372bc1e3a6`; Venus pins Orbit `ea9fd28ce0908f218cf65d4e6df368f0a4e565f5`.
- Full Beads searches for `autoscroll`, `auto-scroll`, `selection scroll`, and `drag scrollback` found only closed issues that deliberately excluded this behavior; no existing implementation bead owns it.

## Ownership and split

1. Create and complete one Eon Sessions child first. Orbit owns an atomic bounded selection-plus-upward-viewport transition, terminal-versus-host routing, authoritative edge detection, revisions, selected frames, frozen copy, synchronized-output behavior, and pressure semantics. Ordinary ORB-C8 scrolling must retain its existing selection-clearing contract.
2. Only from the exact accepted Orbit proof, create and complete one Eon Desktop child. Venus owns transient top-edge intent, native pointer/release/focus delivery, wakeup cadence, presentation, and clipboard effects. It must not infer the Orbit route, cache history, or reconstruct selection content.
3. Add full-Eon installed acceptance only if the exact Orbit/Venus pin changes require downstream composition proof. Eon owns no scrolling or selection mechanism.

Do not implement this epic directly or edit both repositories in one child.

## Reference gate

Required before the Orbit child:

- Read complete ORB-C8, ORB-C9, current ORBS codec/bounds, vertical preview/commit, selection gesture, synchronized-output deferral, output-queue admission, and lifecycle proofs.
- Inspect pinned `libghostty-vt` 0.2.1 and Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083` for tracked selection behavior across authoritative viewport movement. Establish with a disposable focused probe whether the public API can preserve one gesture while the viewport moves.
- Inspect one exact mature terminal implementation with upward drag-edge autoscroll for cadence, edge, release, and terminal-mouse routing comparison. Adopt behavior only; copy no code or configuration surface.

Required before the Venus child:

- Read accepted owner contract/proof, VEN-C2/VEN-C7, `TerminalScroll`, `SelectionGate`, deferred-selection ordering, presentation invalidation, pointer capture/focus loss, resize, and Application scheduling.
- Inspect exact pinned winit event and control-flow behavior on Linux Wayland and the accepted macOS feasibility evidence available at implementation time.

Rejected up front: client-owned rows or anchors, local terminal-mode inference, combining ordinary wheel scrolling with selection, polling threads, configurable speed, acceleration curves, a generic gesture framework, a second renderer/model, and any new dependency.

## Scope

In scope:

- Upward autoscroll only, beginning at the top visible terminal row during an active left-pointer sequence.
- One explicit bounded Orbit semantic transition that can preserve and extend a host selection without changing ordinary scroll behavior.
- One in-flight operation and deterministic stop at the retained-history edge.
- Existing cell, word, and logical-line drag granularity in both selection directions.
- Compatible live output, synchronized output, wide/combining text, soft wraps, resize/reflow, release copy, cancellation, reconnect, and pressure boundaries.
- Platform-neutral protocol and core state. Prove current Linux Wayland behavior; keep the existing macOS path credible without claiming support.

Out of scope:

- Downward edge autoscroll, horizontal scrolling, manual wheel input during selection, speed settings, acceleration, block/rectangular selection, custom separators, semantic command regions, search, graphics selection, new clipboard behavior, or another history store.
- Eon-owned selection logic, a compatibility adapter, dual ORBS support, remote/multiple clients, packaging, signing, or a new platform promise.

## Implementation notes

1. Split this epic only when the user activates the work and the one-active-frontier rule permits it.
2. In Orbit, write one red authoritative interaction check first. Select the smallest public libghostty-backed transition and one canonical bounded wire action/result; preserve the existing manual-scroll clearing contract.
3. Prove Orbit before changing Venus. Publish one exact breaking consumer update order with no compatibility window.
4. In Venus, add the smallest transient edge state beside the existing pointer/application owner. Reuse the existing event-loop deadline and one-in-flight flow; use a fixed bounded cadence with no setting or acceleration.
5. Send edge intent without route inference. After each accepted authoritative frame, continue only while the button is held at the top edge and more history exists; stop immediately on every cancellation boundary.
6. Update contract/reference/current-state docs, changelog only after accepted runtime behavior, and each repository LOC scorecard for tracked source changes.

## Verification

- Orbit focused red/green check: begin a host cell/word/line selection, repeatedly extend upward across more than one viewport of retained Unicode history, reach the oldest edge, release, and assert exact selected presentation and frozen copied text.
- Orbit controls: ordinary `ScrollVertical` still clears selection; terminal-routed mouse mode emits no host autoscroll; synchronized output, stale/future revision, pressure, resize, detach, and alternate screen remain bounded and ordered.
- Venus focused Application check: top-edge hold produces at most one in-flight semantic request, accepted frames advance the same gesture, and release/focus loss/cursor loss/resize/reconnect/edge stop all future requests without losing the final phase.
- Native x86_64 Linux Wayland dogfood: drag from visible text through multiple screens of older history during quiet and compatible live output, then verify exact copy and prompt stop on release and at the oldest edge.
- Run each changed repository's required locked Rust and Nix route once on the unchanged candidate; full Eon installed proof is required only if composition pins change.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if current ORB-C8/ORB-C9 or the exact consumer pins have materially changed.
- Stop and return to the user if the public libghostty API cannot preserve one authoritative gesture across viewport movement without dependency/fork work.
- Stop if a correct shape requires Venus to infer terminal modes, own history/selection content, or coordinate ordinary scroll plus selection as two non-atomic messages.
- Stop before adding a dependency, compatibility window, generic framework, configurable policy, or additional direction.
- Stop before implementation while another production frontier owns the affected Orbit or Venus interaction surface.

## Maintenance notes

Priority is P1 because this removes a daily terminal-selection dead end, but the epic remains deferred and unclaimed until explicitly activated. Dependency decision: no new dependency is selected; first prove the capability with the existing libghostty, Orbit protocol owner, winit loop, and Venus rendering/input stack.

title: Separate native focus from Orbit input generations
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens existing `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C3`, and `VEN-C8`; it adds or changes no product contract. Consumes Orbit `ORB-C1`, `ORB-C3`, `ORB-C5`, and `ORB-C7` through canonical ORBS v4 at accepted proof and exact pinned package revision `7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c`, and Eon `EON-C10` at accepted proof `4af395aea06c230ee6b18cf0755ae25915c0b88d`. Stop for user approval if the accepted producer boundary cannot retire an old client generation without a protocol change.

This issue is open and unclaimed. Before claiming, reconfirm that no other implementation owns the active cross-repository frontier and rebaseline against all accepted producer revisions.

## Why

Consumers: `InputState`, Application workspace focus, and Orbit attachment lifecycle. Triggers: native window focus changes, internal terminal/tab/pane focus changes, endpoint replacement, and transport loss/recovery. Result: native keyboard state and per-terminal capture state have distinct owners; internal focus does not erase still-held native modifiers, and no key, button, shortcut, composition, selection, or semantic focus transition crosses an Orbit generation or remains stale after an undeliverable release. Important failures: do not send unmatched releases or held-button motion into a different terminal, and do not leave the old terminal focused when Venus switches away.

The audit `ven-audit-venus-input-effects-oks` found two symptoms with one root owner. `InputState::focus(false)` is the only full reset, so internal workspace focus incorrectly clears native modifiers, while attachment and loss transitions clear only scroll/selection and leave other per-generation state alive.

Effort M. Implementation risk MED. Confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `src/input.rs:16-27`: one state object mixes native modifiers with per-terminal composition, pressed buttons, and shortcut captures.
- `src/input.rs:56-70`: `focus(false)` clears every transient, including the native modifier snapshot.
- `src/input.rs:370-386`: shortcut release pairing persists in capture vectors until an observed release.
- `src/main.rs:268-303`: internal workspace focus uses the same reset as native focus; endpoint replacement drops transport but resets only scroll and selection.
- `src/main.rs:364-418`: workspace shortcuts can cause an endpoint change while modifiers remain held.
- `src/main.rs:493-508,808-845`: transport loss and native input routing can reject a release without retiring all related state.
- Accepted Orbit `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174` disconnect cleanup clears selection but does not synthesize focus or key/button releases.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/input.rs` lifecycle ownership and the minimum state required for native focus, terminal-region focus, attachment generation, key/button pairing, shortcut capture, and IME composition.
- `src/main.rs` transitions for native focus, workspace focus, endpoint replacement, transport loss, reconnect, and semantic focus replay.
- Focused deterministic tests plus existing canonical interaction and lifecycle tests.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof revisions for VEN-C2/VEN-C3/VEN-C8 after a committed source candidate, README LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG only for the accepted user-visible corrections.

Out of scope:
- Orbit or Eon schema changes, PTY ownership, replay/ack infrastructure, a generic input framework, global shortcut configuration, richer focus regions, and dependencies.
- Changing the documented workspace shortcut set or terminal key encoding.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code: reread this Bead and comments; `docs/REFERENCES.md` input, paste, workspace, and lifecycle entries; exact Orbit source/proofs above including disconnect and semantic focus/key/mouse handling; exact Eon workspace producer proof; current InputState/Application/Transport owners; exact winit 0.30.13 focus, modifier, keyboard, IME, and pointer event semantics. Record the execution baseline and append-only Reference gate before edits.

Comparison-only: prior Alacritty 0.15.1 evidence may inform native focus cleanup only where the exact question and revision still match. Reject its terminal/grid/configuration ownership and all source reuse. No manifest edit or dependency is expected; stop for the crate gate and user approval if one becomes necessary.

Platform disposition: isolated existing winit dependency. Keep policy neutral above native events; Linux is the proof target, while macOS event ordering remains unproved and must not be inferred.

## Implementation notes

1. First add failing state-transition tests for: held Ctrl across terminal-to-workspace-to-terminal focus; endpoint replacement between press and release; same-endpoint loss with a release while transport is absent; held mouse button across loss; shortcut capture and IME composition across generations; and native window focus loss.
2. Separate native-window state from terminal-region semantic focus and per-Orbit-generation capture. Reuse InputState and Application rather than adding a new module or framework.
3. Give attachment/transport transitions one owner that retires old per-terminal state before the new generation accepts native input. Preserve native modifier truth unless the native window actually loses focus.
4. Keep focus, key, mouse, selection, paste, and workspace shortcut ordering deterministic. Do not manufacture terminal bytes or compensate for hidden Orbit state.
5. Preserve current bounded queue failure visibility and latest-focus replay only for the current generation.

title: Separate transport loss state from retry policy
description:
## Contract routing

Hardens existing `VEN-C3` and `VEN-C4`; it adds or changes no product contract. Consumes Orbit `ORB-C3`, `ORB-C4`, and `ORB-C7` plus canonical ORBS v4 at accepted proof and exact pinned package revision `7f067b30e97d0b4787a7c6c0bbe3dd8a80a61c2c`. Stop for user approval if the correction requires a new connection state contract or changed Orbit failure semantics.

This issue is open and unclaimed. Before claiming, reconfirm that no other implementation owns the active cross-repository frontier and rebaseline against the exact accepted Orbit proofs.

## Why

Consumer: the Venus connection status and semantic input gate. Trigger: a Protocol or Terminal failure suppresses retry, a later accepted Orbit result clears that notice, and the local transport then reports retryable socket loss. Result: every ended transport must move the client to an explicit non-attached state, while a separate policy decides whether recovery is scheduled. Important failure: Venus must never appear attached or silently accept native input when no transport exists.

The audit `ven-audit-venus-input-effects-oks` proved that one `retryable_loss` boolean currently controls both loss recording and retry scheduling. When retry is suppressed, `mark_lost` is skipped but the transport is still removed.

Effort S. Implementation risk MED. Confidence HIGH.

## Evidence

- `src/main.rs:449-461`: Protocol or Terminal failures set `retry_suppressed`, and `retryable_loss` becomes false when suppression is active.
- `src/main.rs:493-513`: the same boolean gates `model.mark_lost`, while every transport end removes the transport.
- `src/main.rs:589-594`: an Attached model with no transport rejects input without a notice.
- `src/model.rs:168-170,222-235,266-273`: attachment state gates input; `Accepted` clears the Orbit failure notice; `mark_lost` owns the visible Lost transition.
- Accepted Orbit source `3ee7c80005f3d2bbe81e539799327803716f6174:src/main.rs:651-680` can emit a non-closing Terminal failure and later Accepted, so the sequence is reachable without speculative producer behavior.

## Scope

In scope:
- `src/main.rs` transport-end transition and retry scheduling policy.
- `src/model.rs` only if the existing Lost transition cannot preserve the required visible reason without duplicate state.
- The narrowest deterministic state-sequence tests, plus existing retry/model/transport tests.
- `docs/CONTRACTS.md` proof revisions for VEN-C3/VEN-C4 after a committed source candidate, README LOC scorecard, and CHANGELOG only for the accepted user-visible correction.

Out of scope:
- Orbit changes, new retry modes, backoff changes, remote transport, automatic recovery after authoritative terminal/protocol failure, protocol adapters, and dependencies.
- Refactoring transport framing or queue ownership.

## Reference and dependency gate

Required before code: reread this Bead and comments; `docs/REFERENCES.md` lifecycle and failure entries; exact Orbit proofs and current pinned source above, especially closing versus non-closing Failure paths; current Application, SessionModel, and TransportEvent owners; prior `ven-upt.3` evidence at its exact revisions. Record the execution baseline and append-only Reference gate before edits.

Comparison references are rejected because the accepted producer and local state machine fully specify this bug. No manifest edit or dependency is expected; stop for the crate gate and user approval if one becomes necessary.

Platform disposition: neutral. This is a local state-machine invariant with no platform-specific branch; Linux remains the proof environment and no macOS claim is added.

## Implementation notes

1. First make a deterministic test fail for Terminal Failure, Accepted, then RetryableLoss, asserting model state, notice, transport absence, retry schedule, and input gate.
2. Separate the unconditional transport-ended state transition from the conditional retry-scheduling decision at their existing Application owner. Use the existing SessionModel Lost state unless evidence proves it insufficient.
3. Preserve terminal/protocol retry suppression, same-selected-live endpoint retry eligibility, last coherent scene retention, and bounded backoff.
4. Ensure every no-transport state has explicit bounded client-visible status and cannot pass `is_attached` input gates.
5. Commit and verify the source candidate first; then advance VEN-C3/VEN-C4 proof metadata, update the LOC scorecard and applicable changelog, close the Bead against the source commit, and commit metadata plus closure together.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Failure(Terminal) -> Accepted -> RetryableLoss` cannot leave SessionModel Attached.
- A suppressed loss records an explicit non-attached state and schedules no retry.
- An ordinary eligible RetryableLoss still records Lost, retains the coherent scene, and schedules the existing bounded retry.
- Busy, Incompatible, Exited, Protocol, terminal, authoritative offline, endpoint replacement, and queue/worker failure behavior remain unchanged except for eliminating attached-without-transport.
- Input and paste cannot silently operate against an absent transport.
- No new connection-state owner, retry mode, dependency, or compatibility surface is added.

## Verification

- Focused state-sequence tests must cover suppressed and eligible loss, failure notice clearing, retry scheduling, and input gating.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

All commands must exit 0 on the materially unchanged source candidate; record test counts, environment, and exact Orbit proof identity.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the current accepted Orbit failure lifecycle differs from the recorded source; rebaseline against the new accepted proof.
- Stop if preserving the constraining failure reason requires changing VEN-C3/VEN-C4, adding an Orbit field, or adding a compatibility state.
- Stop rather than re-enabling retries for authoritative Protocol or Terminal failures.

## Maintenance notes

Connection state and retry policy are separate invariants. The minimum fix keeps their existing owners and prevents one policy boolean from suppressing both. Cheapest falsifier: Terminal Failure, Accepted, RetryableLoss must yield visible non-attached state, absent transport, and no scheduled retry.

title: Present tool popups and the project chooser through one Venus surface
description:
## Outcome
Materialize Eon's accepted popup state in one native tab-body surface, shared by terminal tools and the Alt+Z/startup/new-tab chooser. Cover the complete accordion stack while retaining the tab strip; preserve Orbit's terminal and input authority.

## Prerequisites
Part of Eon epic eon-tool-popups-e13. Prerequisite eon-tool-popups-e13.4 is accepted at exact source 0cc8f477298681ae3945903e8fdb5852d487c5ab, after lifecycle/configuration decision eon-tool-popups-e13.1. This consumer precedes Eon runtime activation in eon-tool-popups-e13.2. Eon owns policy; consume its published schema/actions instead of reconstructing them. Reconcile the external blocker only from the exact owner proof and source, not a compatible-looking draft. No speculative Orbit APIs.

## Contract routing and reference gate
Refine VEN-C8 and VEN-C18 as approved by the product decision; preserve VEN-C1/C2/C3/C4/C11/C15/C19 and standalone behavior. Record current exact accepted Eon/Orbit contracts before implementation. Platform classification: isolated Wayland dependency.
Required before code: this repository's docs/REFERENCES.md and applicable exact sources; scene.rs picker/tab-body geometry, application.rs attachment/focus/input and render.rs frame/background paths; Eon's accepted popup contract and its reference route. Required comparisons: Nova 6575ae476a8d4b2fa8b4aa8d0f3839bdba6467e1 popup/chooser/full-Yazi roles, Zellij Popup f9424823b01e5223dadff9e6c5b87c0131a902f8 geometry and the exact Kitty overlay source routed by Eon docs/REFERENCES.md. Inspect licenses before reuse. References do not authorize plugin, layout-engine or terminal-state adoption.

## Acceptance
- One native presentation path consumes Eon's selected popup endpoint and replaces the complete stack, including all pane headers, without creating stack rows. The chooser uses this path; Venus neither recognizes its search/browser modes nor applies separate product-lifecycle rules.
- Keep tabs visible. Use the agreed available-body calculation; future accepted sidebar work can supply remaining width without reserving an absent rail. Do not implement or claim sidebar reflow before a sidebar exists.
- Visually review the parent proposal: 8 logical pixels per side, 4 above/below, rounded frame, thin brighter border, small integrated label, and continuous default background/opacity under existing blur. Record justified spacing adjustments; clamp tiny geometry without clipped or invalid input regions.
- Geometry, terminal resize, clipping, hit testing, focus/accessibility and IME agree. Only the visible Session receives typing/paste/pointer input. App-owned Escape/Ctrl+C/Tab reach the terminal; semantic popup shortcuts follow Eon's accepted actions. Resizing does not restart a tool.
- Share the current single-terminal attachment path; no requirement to draw a live terminal behind the popup. Preserve previous-pane restoration under Eon policy, endpoint loss/failure handling, standalone raw keys and picker-first admission with no placeholder pane.
- Prove deterministic projection/input boundaries and one isolated native normal/narrow-window observation using the exact accepted Eon protocol seed with a bounded substitute workspace producer and real accepted Orbit Sessions. This proves the Venus surface, not installed full-Eon policy. Complete affected Rust/Nix checks and publish exact source/proof for downstream Eon delivery; qualify fractional scale, compositor blur and any unexercised accessibility surface.

## Scope
Venus native presentation and exact owned dependency consumption only. No Eon command selection, cwd replacement, settings parser, pending-tab lifecycle, Orbit parser/state, second schema/emulator, generic popup/plugin framework, sidebar, external desktop window or broad platform support. The user activated this consumer and its VEN-C8/C18 refinement; implementation and verification are confined to this issue.

## External prerequisites
- eon:eon-tool-popups-e13.4 — exact accepted shared-popup protocol seed; includes decision eon-tool-popups-e13.1.

Do not depend on Eon runtime activation: that would create a cross-repository cycle. Keep the current installed Eon composition on its existing Venus pin until eon-tool-popups-e13.2 coherently activates the new runtime and exact accepted consumer. Publish the consumer's exact source and qualified native/protocol proof for that activation.

title: Keep cursor blink cadence stable during active output
description:
## Why

While Codex is working in Eonova, the terminal cursor visibly flickers much faster than the intended blink cadence. The owning layer is not yet proved. Nova/Zellij may emit rapid cursor controls, Orbit may publish rapid canonical cursor changes, or Venus may add transitions in native presentation. Diagnose that boundary first and fix only the confirmed owner.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a local user viewing an attached Orbit session through Venus.
- Trigger: frequent terminal updates while the canonical cursor remains visible and blinking.
- Result: content revisions remain prompt, while cursor visibility changes only for authoritative cursor-state changes or Venus's stable blink cadence.
- Important failures: hidden and non-blinking canonical cursor states remain exact. Venus must not drop frames, ignore cursor controls, or special-case Codex to hide the symptom.

Contract routing:
- Hardens proved VEN-C1; no new Venus contract is proposed.
- Preserves VEN-C2, VEN-C3, VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, and candidate VEN-C9.
- Consumes canonical ORBS v2 at accepted Orbit proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`.
- Changes no Orbit or Eon contract. A confirmed upstream cause produces an evidence-backed handoff, not an edit or issue in another repository.

## Evidence

- User observation on 2026-08-10: the cursor repeatedly flickers while Codex works in the installed Eonova composition.
- Observed environment: active Eonova profile `91a31a8772d74d89f8a9399df1338c592ef0c1e6` at `/nix/store/3xnb1pd547mw6rf9gppwvn9ndm3b20z6-eonova-0.1.0`; it pins Eon `ec0fa0fd0bb6d78a0d37281b069899d1bd13b95e` and Nova `6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd`. That Eon revision consumes Orbit `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169` and Venus `690b038e2b58a0e7761023ac7e004e92327ac901`; Codex CLI is 0.147.0.
- `src/main.rs` defines a 500 ms half-period. `update_blink` starts one deadline, toggles only when that deadline is due, then schedules another full interval. Calling this helper more often cannot itself create faster transitions.
- `Application::handle_transport` accepts Orbit frames and requests redraws. `src/scene.rs` copies Orbit's `cursor.visible` and `cursor.blinking` values unchanged, and `src/render.rs` combines those values with the local blink phase.
- Orbit's `presentation.rs` extracts visibility and blinking from each Ghostty snapshot and publishes complete coalescible frames after changed PTY turns. The cursor values and presentation timestamps during the reported workload have not been captured.
- Existing tests prove blink metadata propagation and a complete visible phase after idle. They do not distinguish authoritative cursor changes from native presentation changes during dense output.
- The separate `ven-render-braille-progress-wcf` issue covers Codex's animated Braille activity glyph. Reproduction must confirm this report concerns the cursor rectangle rather than that changing terminal cell.

Impact: MED for sustained Codex dogfooding and basic presentation quality.
Effort: S if Venus owns the transition; M if evidence must be handed to Orbit.
Risk: MED because suppressing legitimate cursor controls or delaying content would violate terminal fidelity.
Confidence: HIGH in the observed symptom; MED in its owner until the timeline is captured.

## Scope

In scope:
- Reproduce first in the exact Eonova profile, then through isolated plain `eon terminal -- COMMAND` with the same Eon/Venus generation and controlled dense output, then exact Codex 0.147.0.
- Capture accepted frame revision/timestamp plus `cursor.visible` and `cursor.blinking`; distinguish the cursor rectangle from changing content beneath or beside it.
- If canonical cursor state stays stable, capture Venus's effective cursor-visible predicate at successful presentations and inspect the existing host scheduler.
- Correct the smallest confirmed Venus owner and add one regression at that owner.
- Update VEN-C1 proof metadata, current-state docs, changelog when behavior changes, and README LOC for a Venus correction.

Out of scope:
- Codex-specific rules, terminal-output parsing, configurable blink settings, changing the 500 ms interval as a workaround, a general animation scheduler, frame throttling, renderer replacement, protocol changes, dependencies, or cross-repository edits.
- Creating an Orbit issue or changing another audit dependency without separate user authorization.
- Hidden/non-blinking cursor semantics, text blinking semantics, PTY authority, input, workspace topology, and window-decoration behavior.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current `AGENTS.md`, VEN-C1 and preserved contracts, `docs/CRATES.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and the complete current Venus cursor/blink flow and tests.
- Eonova `91a31a8772d74d89f8a9399df1338c592ef0c1e6`, pinned Eon `ec0fa0fd0bb6d78a0d37281b069899d1bd13b95e`, and Nova `6c7174b4efca5f139a461d204186c5001d6457bd` for the exact dogfood composition.
- Exact accepted Orbit proof `9d6d2bb37f20ab4ad9e186c7bc715eabef43e757`, installed producer `64db581445bafca1a08a6530f8e44f9c1edbc169`, and its snapshot-to-frame cursor path.

Conditional:
- Exact winit 0.30.13 wait/redraw semantics only if stable canonical frames still produce a too-fast Venus presentation timeline.
- Exact Orbit-pinned Ghostty cursor semantics only if Orbit frames author the rapid changes.
- Exact Codex 0.147.0 source only if captured output cannot establish which cursor controls or updates cause the difference.

Rejected:
- Always showing the cursor, ignoring canonical visibility, slowing every redraw, dropping accepted frames, per-application detection, or adding a second cursor-state owner.

Platform classification: isolated native scheduling if Venus owns the defect; otherwise neutral protocol production. Prove Linux first. macOS and broader compositor timing remain unproved.

## Implementation Notes

1. Claim and baseline this Bead after the active window-decoration Bead is committed because both may touch `src/main.rs`.
2. Record the canonical frame cursor timeline for controlled dense output and Codex in Eonova and isolated plain Eon. If rapid changes are already canonical, distinguish explicit application cursor controls from Orbit publication behavior and stop at that owning boundary.
3. If canonical values are stable, record successful Venus presentation times and the effective cursor-visible predicate. The existing `update_blink` helper is already bounded by direct inspection, so do not add a dense-call test unless a confirmed correction changes that owner.
4. Add the cheapest failing regression for the actual defect and fix it in the existing owner. Add no timer abstraction or renderer policy unless evidence requires one.
5. Run locked checks and dogfood the distribution-equivalent Eon runtime. Repeat the revised-state review after any correction.

## Verification

- The pre-fix capture identifies each visible transition as canonical cursor metadata, Venus blink phase, or changing content mistaken for the cursor.
- If Venus owns the defect, one regression fails before and passes after at the confirmed scheduler/presentation seam.
- Controlled content remains prompt; hidden and non-blinking cursors remain exact; no transition attributed to Venus occurs faster than the selected half-period.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native Eonova and isolated plain-Eon COSMIC Wayland dogfood record exact runtime revisions and the observed cursor-transition bound for controlled output and Codex working/idle states.
- Advance VEN-C1 only at an immutable proof-bearing Venus commit; retain the Orbit proof unless Orbit owns the defect.

## Stop Conditions

- Eonova-only reproduction is not owner proof. Stop Venus work only when captured application controls or accepted Orbit frames already contain the rapid transitions; route to Orbit only when its snapshot or publication behavior is the confirmed owner.
- Stop and report if controlled output is stable but exact Codex output intentionally requests the observed transitions; do not special-case it in Venus.
- Stop if the symptom is the Braille activity glyph rather than the cursor; `ven-render-braille-progress-wcf` already owns that defect.
- Stop for user approval before a new contract, dependency, protocol change, frame-rate policy, cross-repository edit, upstream issue, or additional audit dependency.
- Rebaseline after the active window-decoration implementation because it changes the native host surface.

## Maintenance Notes

Content traffic and cursor presentation have distinct owners: accepted frames author terminal state; Venus supplies only the bounded phase for canonically blinking content. This issue and `ven-render-braille-progress-wcf` independently block `ven-audit-venus-scene-renderer-2db`. If reproduction proves a Venus host-scheduler defect, report that `ven-audit-venus-host-lifecycle-8jl` should also depend on this issue before its audit begins.
close_reason: Obsolete by user decision on 2026-08-12. Current Eonova presents a steady cursor: Orbit publishes libghostty's canonical blink state, whose unset default is non-blinking, and Venus already supplies a bounded 500 ms phase only when that state is blinking. Eon deliberately keeps the steady default while preserving explicit application-requested blinking. The earlier rapid-flicker symptom is no longer reproducible and no Venus scheduler defect was established. No replacement Orbit issue is needed.

title: Apply terminal background opacity
description:
## Approved outcome and contract

The user approved this opacity-first shape on 2026-08-14 America/Sao_Paulo. This implementation creates `VEN-C11` after indexing the approved contract before code.

- Consumer: Eon or EonTerm launching one Venus surface through the accepted component boundary.
- Trigger: launch with `--background-opacity VALUE`, or launch directly with no value.
- Result: a finite value in `0.0..=1.0` controls only the terminal default background. No value is equivalent to `1.0` and preserves current presentation. The active Orbit frame background, including later color changes, and otherwise empty terminal padding use the configured alpha. Explicit cell backgrounds, selection, inverse video, workspace chrome, notices, and focus borders remain opaque. Text, cursor, underline, preedit, accessibility, and input retain their current semantics.
- Failures: malformed, non-finite, or out-of-range values fail during launch parsing. A value below `1.0` fails explicitly before the hidden window becomes visible when the selected surface lacks a proved premultiplied alpha mode; Venus never silently falls back to opaque output.

This creates `VEN-C11`, changes and proves `VEN-C1`, and preserves `VEN-C2`, `VEN-C3`, `VEN-C4`, `VEN-C7`, `VEN-C8`, `VEN-C9`, `VEN-C10`, `VEN-C12`, `VEN-C13`, and `VEN-C14`. Eon owns persistence, product defaults, schema, and composition. Venus revalidates its launch boundary and owns native materialization. Orbit remains unaware of opacity and continues to own terminal colors and state.

Impact: HIGH. Effort: M. Implementation risk: MED. Confidence: HIGH in the Linux shape and native capabilities; macOS remains an explicit blocker below.

## Evidence

- Venus `4f799fef1c3e10e86d70b708708f7c2702d7aee8`, `src/render.rs:193-207`: surface initialization overwrites the supported default with `CompositeAlphaMode::Opaque`, which ignores alpha.
- `src/render.rs:472-545`: workspace and standalone paths have distinct clear/background ownership; workspace terminal background is currently an opaque rectangle.
- `src/render.rs:1239-1263`: cell backgrounds are skipped by resolved RGB equality, so an explicit background equal to the terminal default is currently indistinguishable from a default background.
- `src/scene.rs:671-727`: Orbit style colors are resolved to RGB and inverse/selection are applied before rendering; opacity must remain separate from the canonical Orbit scene color.
- Exact locked winit 0.30.13 requires the transparent hint at window creation for X11 and treats it as a native compositing hint.
- Exact locked wgpu 30.0.0 defines `Auto` as opaque-or-inherit, `Opaque` as ignoring alpha, and `PreMultiplied` as requiring RGB already multiplied by alpha.
- A disposable exact-version native probe on 2026-08-14 found COSMIC Wayland Vulkan capabilities `[Opaque, PreMultiplied]` and Xwayland `[PreMultiplied, Inherit]` on Intel RPL-S. The probe was removed after observation.
- Mars `2b63717135a72ef330d8c2da8ca4cde59c22d739` and Ghostty `a887df42c56f6de86c0fe6da9c4eeca37931e083`, both MIT comparison-only evidence, converge on default-background opacity while explicit backgrounds, selection, and inverse presentation remain opaque unless a separate cell-opacity option is enabled.
- Nova `446d2e25db8a43dac8f30dc21d1e4519cb5c9526` selects Mars opacity `0.88` with `opacity-cells = false`.

## Minimum implementation

1. Extend the existing launch parser with one `f32` scalar. Keep direct no-option launch at `1.0`; add no profile object, config file, environment variable, module, or dependency.
2. Set winit transparency before window creation exactly when opacity is below `1.0`. Do not add live mutation; X11 cannot reliably change this after creation.
3. For opacity `1.0`, retain wgpu `Auto` so an Inherit-only opaque surface remains valid. For opacity below `1.0`, choose reported `PreMultiplied`; otherwise return one bounded startup error. Do not select unsupported `Opaque` or unproved `PostMultiplied`.
4. Keep the existing straight-source alpha blend pipelines. Premultiply only translucent clear RGB after its current sRGB-to-linear conversion. In workspace mode clear transparent, draw the terminal viewport background at the configured alpha, and leave the already-owned chrome rectangles opaque. In standalone mode clear to the active scene background at the configured alpha.
5. Retain one renderer-facing provenance bit on each resolved style indicating a true terminal-default background. Any explicit style background remains explicit even when its RGB equals the frame background. Selection or inverse presentation is never classified as default. Group and skip background runs using that provenance, not RGB equality alone.
6. Keep `SceneColor` RGB-only and consume unchanged exact Orbit frames. Reuse the stored valid surface configuration for resize and Lost recovery.
7. After an immutable source candidate, update contract proof metadata, README LOC, and CHANGELOG for the accepted visible behavior, then close through the repository source-proof workflow.

No new shader, offscreen texture, render pipeline, renderer abstraction, crate, protocol field, or Venus module is part of the Linux slice.

## Layer policy

- Configured alpha: terminal default background, current Orbit frame background, empty terminal viewport, and standalone terminal padding.
- Opaque: explicit cell backgrounds, including an explicit color equal to the default; selected or inverse cells; Eon tab and pane chrome; focus borders; status notices.
- Unchanged current alpha: foreground glyph antialiasing, faint text, block cursor, underline, preedit, and other existing foreground effects.
- Platform-owned: native decorations, titlebar, shadow, compositor policy, and input region. Visual transparency does not imply click-through.

## References and dependency disposition

Required before code: current `AGENTS.md`; complete issue and comments; current `docs/CONTRACTS.md`, `docs/REFERENCES.md`, and `docs/CRATES.md`; proved VEN-C1/VEN-C2/VEN-C7/VEN-C8 owners; current launch, window, scene, renderer, workspace, accessibility, IME, resize, and recovery paths; exact locked winit/wgpu/glyphon sources cited above; exact accepted Eon launch/config boundary; and the exact Mars/Ghostty/Nova comparison identities above.

No dependency or crate change is selected. A manifest edit requires a fresh crate gate and user approval.

Platform disposition: isolated platform dependency. Linux Wayland and Xwayland are the first proof targets. Exact wgpu Metal 30 advertises only `Opaque` and `PostMultiplied`; correct PostMultiplied output would require an equivalent proven conversion, likely a final unpremultiplication pass of roughly 150-250 Rust lines plus native Metal proof. That is a macOS blocker, not part of this issue.

## Acceptance

1. The approved `VEN-C11` row and exact Eon compatibility order are indexed before code.
2. No-option and explicit `1.0` launch preserve current accepted output. Values `0.0`, `0.88`, and `1.0` parse; malformed, NaN, infinity, and out-of-range values fail deterministically before the window is visible.
3. Opacity below `1.0` requests a transparent winit window and selects only reported `PreMultiplied`. Opacity `1.0` does not force an unsupported alpha mode. Surface resize, Outdated/Suboptimal recovery, and Lost recreation retain a valid stored configuration.
4. The active Orbit background follows the configured alpha across ordinary frames and dynamic background changes. Default cell runs do not repaint it.
5. Explicit backgrounds remain opaque even when equal to the terminal background. Selection and inverse presentation remain opaque. Foreground, cursor, IME, input, hit testing, selection geometry, and accessibility remain exact.
6. Workspace terminal content is translucent while tabs, pane headers, borders, notices, and native-decoration ownership remain unchanged. Standalone EonTerm and workspace Venus agree on terminal-background semantics.
7. Focused tests cover scalar bounds, alpha-mode selection, premultiplied clear values, default-versus-explicit provenance, explicit same-RGB backgrounds, selection/inverse, workspace layer policy, default parity, and recovery configuration.
8. Native COSMIC Wayland and Xwayland dogfood covers `1.0`, `0.88`, and `0.0`; decorated and undecorated windows; standalone and workspace paths; resize; active background changes; shell, Helix/Neovim, Yazi, and tmux-style explicit backgrounds; selection; inverse; cursor; status notice; reconnect; and compositor-visible transparency.
9. Closure records exact revisions, commands, native environment, supported alpha modes, screenshots or observations, dependency disposition, owned LOC, portability blocker, and remaining compositor limits.

## Verification

- Focused deterministic tests must fail on the current forced-Opaque and lost-provenance behavior and pass on the accepted shape.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

All commands must exit 0 on one materially unchanged source candidate. Native proof must name Wayland versus Xwayland and must not imply macOS support.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if correct Linux output requires `PostMultiplied`, an offscreen resolve, another renderer pipeline, a dependency, a manifest edit, or an Orbit/Eon workspace protocol change.
- Stop for user choice before adding explicit-cell opacity, blur, background images, workspace-wide glass, click-through, live reload, a public EonTerm CLI override, or a macOS implementation.
- Stop if the evidence changes the Eon/Venus ownership boundary or another active issue owns the affected launch, scene, or renderer surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

The separate `ven-use-supported-surface-alpha-1tb` finding is implemented by this issue: opaque launch retains supported `Auto`, while transparent launch selects a proved reported mode. Do not implement both issues independently. The deferred typography and initial-geometry outcome is tracked separately and must not expand this slice.

title: Apply terminal typography and initial geometry settings
description:
## Outcome

Apply the approved VEN-C19 startup typography and initial geometry options through Venus’s existing font and cell-grid owners. Venus is proved first; Eon and EonTerm persistence remains the separate eon-terminal-typography-geometry-config-b63 issue.

The user approved the new `VEN-C19` contract, exact bounds, Venus-first order and direct unicode-script =0.5.8 edge on 2026-09-08. `VEN-C11` remains the opacity contract. The canonical startup contract is indexed in docs/CONTRACTS.md.

- Consumer: Eon or EonTerm launching one Venus surface.
- Trigger: launch with accepted typed typography and geometry values, or no overrides.
- Result: Venus applies the values through the one authoritative grid consumed by rendering, resize, pointer mapping, selection, accessibility, cursor anchoring, and IME placement. Absence preserves the accepted 16 px, 10 by 18 logical-cell fallback and current geometry.
- Failures: malformed, non-finite, out-of-range, unavailable, or internally inconsistent values fail before terminal presentation/attachment and never silently fall back. Native output admission may require an initial window buffer before the compositor supplies its scale.

Impact: MED/HIGH. Effort: L. Implementation risk: MED/HIGH because text fitting and every geometry consumer meet here. Confidence: HIGH that the outcome is independently schedulable; field bounds and contract identity are approved and indexed as VEN-C19.

## Evidence

- Closed `ven-0o6` proves the current no-profile 16 logical-pixel text, 10 by 18 logical-cell metrics, shared geometry owner, and native acceptance.
- `src/render.rs` owns `CellMetrics`, font fitting, glyphon buffers, rendering, hit geometry, and initial logical size.
- `src/main.rs`, input, selection, IME, accessibility, and workspace materialization all consume those authoritative metrics.
- The former description of `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` bundled these values with opacity. The user approved splitting opacity into the first vertical slice on 2026-08-14 rather than delaying it behind typography and geometry.

## Scope

In scope:
- One accepted Eon-to-Venus startup boundary for primary family, ordered fallbacks, font size, line height, initial columns, and initial rows.
- Existing `CellMetrics`, font selection/fitting, renderer, resize, input mapping, selection, accessibility, cursor, IME, workspace, launch parsing, focused tests, contract proof, README LOC, and accepted user-visible docs/changelog.
- Exact glyphon 0.12.0 and cosmic-text 0.19.0 behavior already selected by the repository.

Out of scope:
- Background opacity, themes, terminal colors, blur, background images, cursor effects, font packaging, live reload, settings UI, arbitrary split layout, Kitty graphics, renderer replacement, macOS support promise, or Orbit protocol changes.
- A generic profile framework, Venus config file, environment-variable-per-setting boundary, or second geometry owner.

## Implementation notes

1. Wait for `ven-terminal-presentation-settings-5y7` to prove the minimal launch/configuration boundary and avoid overlapping its launch/renderer work.
2. Reread all current metric, font, renderer, workspace, input, selection, accessibility, cursor, resize, and IME owners plus the accepted opacity contract.
3. Obtain user approval for the exact contract id, field names, types, bounds, missing-font behavior, and Eon/Venus update order; index it before code.
4. Extend the existing launch boundary directly. Keep `CellMetrics` and the existing font fitter as the sole geometry and typeface owners.
5. Use TDD for pure bounds, scale-factor geometry, fallback ordering, and invalid profiles, then native Linux dogfood for text quality and configured availability.
6. Add no dependency unless the repository crate gate proves existing glyphon/cosmic-text and platform font facilities insufficient and the user approves the choice.
7. Follow the immutable source candidate then proof-metadata/closure workflow.

## Acceptance

- No-profile behavior is identical to the accepted current defaults.
- Primary family and ordered fallbacks resolve deterministically; unavailable required values fail with bounded diagnostics under the approved policy.
- Font size and line height derive one coherent cell grid at scale factors 1.0, 1.25, 1.5, and 2.0.
- Initial columns and rows produce the requested authoritative grid subject only to explicit native size limits.
- Rendering, resize, hit testing, wheel normalization, selection, cursor, IME, accessibility, and workspace materialization consume the same metrics without drift.
- Native Linux proof covers default and configured Latin, Unicode, wide/combining text, Nerd Font symbols, regular/bold/italic, box/Braille, resize, selection, cursor, IME, accessibility, standalone, and workspace paths.
- Exact locked Rust checks, contract proof, docs, LOC accounting, and `git diff --check` pass on one immutable candidate.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`

Focused tests must prove defaults, bounds, fallback ordering, missing-font policy, all named scale factors, initial geometry, and shared consumer geometry.

## Stop conditions

- Stop before code until the exact contract and compatibility order are user-approved and indexed.
- Stop before a dependency, manifest edit, font package, second metric owner, generic profile framework, live watcher, renderer replacement, or Orbit/Eon workspace protocol change.
- Stop if another active issue owns the same launch, CellMetrics, font, renderer, input geometry, accessibility, or IME surfaces.

## Maintenance notes

This issue deliberately excludes opacity. Expand it only for another user-approved typography or initial-geometry field. Broader Mars parity remains a Nova product decision.

Proposed startup contract — awaiting the explicit contract gate — 2026-09-08

Propose new VEN-C19, keeping VEN-C11 solely about opacity. Consumer: direct Venus, Eon or EonTerm launching one native surface. Trigger: optional strict startup options. Result: one configured terminal font chain and cell grid shared by rendering, resize, pointer/selection, wheel normalization, cursor, IME and accessibility. No live reload. Exact proposed options and bounds:
- --font-family FAMILY: optional installed monospace primary family; a nonempty trimmed UTF-8 name of at most 128 bytes without control characters.
- --font-fallback FAMILY: repeatable ordered installed fallback names, same name bounds, at most eight entries. Fallback faces may be proportional; Orbit remains authoritative for cell widths. Named overrides take precedence over built-in specialty fallback, while the no-override symbol/Braille path remains unchanged. Existing platform fallback remains available after the explicit chain.
- --font-size PX: finite f32, 6..=96 logical px, default 16. This is nominal text size applied through the existing cell fitter.
- --line-height MULTIPLIER: finite f32, 1..=3 times nominal text size, default 1.125 (18/16). The row height and cell width are rounded once at physical scale by CellMetrics; configured primary width is measured by the selected shaper.
- --columns N and --rows N: optional positive u16 values. Missing dimensions retain their current initial logical window dimension; the requested terminal grid must fit Orbit's 100,000-cell bound and effective native pixel/GPU bounds. Workspace overhead comes from its existing Scene owner. Compositor placement/tiling/size limits may override the request; actual resize remains authoritative and Venus does not fight later user resizing.

Malformed/non-finite/out-of-range values, duplicate singleton options, unavailable named families, non-monospace primary and impossible admitted initial sizes fail with bounded diagnostics before first presentation/terminal attachment; no silently substituted named font. Font availability does not guarantee every Unicode glyph or style variant. title: Add a toggleable native shortcut viewer to Venus
description:
## Outcome and contract

Create `VEN-C20 — Native shortcut viewer`.

Consumer: one person using a Venus surface attached to a full Eon workspace.

Trigger: the person presses the reserved physical `Alt+Slash` shortcut while the viewer is closed, presses it again while open, or presses Escape while open.

Result: Venus opens and closes one native, read-only shortcut viewer without starting an Orbit Session or changing the Eon workspace. The viewer lists the shortcuts that are actually available from the native Eon surface, grouped for quick scanning:

- navigation and direct positional tab access;
- tab and pane creation, close, movement, and focus;
- enabled Project/tool popup entries from the current EONW v5 snapshot;
- focus cycling, clipboard, and link-opening actions owned by the Venus host.

The list is current rather than hardcoded: fixed Venus bindings have one local descriptor owner shared by dispatch and presentation, while configurable popup rows come directly from `Snapshot.entries`. Disabled or absent entries do not appear. Child applications retain their own bindings and help; the viewer does not claim Helix, Yazi, LazyGit, agent, shell, or arbitrary terminal-application shortcuts.

Important failures: opening or closing the viewer sends no terminal bytes or EONW action. Repeats do not oscillate it. Workspace refresh updates dynamic entries without closing the viewer. Workspace/terminal loss leaves a dismissible native surface and follows existing bounded recovery. Tiny windows, long labels, many configured entries, non-US layouts, focus loss, and accessibility navigation must not trap input or make dismissal unavailable.

User-approved presentation decision, 2026-09-11: use one viewer surface and one data model. Ship toggle/pin first. A momentary peek may later reuse the same renderer and data only if dogfood demonstrates value; add no timer, modifier-only gesture, second renderer, or preparatory abstraction in this slice.

Impact: HIGH for discoverability and learning. Effort: M. Risk: MEDIUM because native input precedence, focus, responsive layout, and accessibility meet in one modal surface. Confidence: HIGH.

## Evidence

- Venus baseline `660abf30363817a7a466121cf63be4bd662d4dd5`; the only existing working-tree change is unrelated Beads state and must be preserved.
- `src/application.rs:1199-1278` owns workspace key precedence and release capture.
- `src/application.rs:2935-3045` separately recognizes fixed workspace, positional-tab, and Eon-supplied popup shortcuts. A viewer must not reproduce these chords in an unrelated display-only list.
- `src/input.rs:445-474` already captures recognized host shortcut press/release pairs so releases do not leak to Orbit after a host action.
- `src/scene.rs:220-580`, `src/render.rs`, and `src/accessibility.rs` own native workspace layout, drawing, focus, and AccessKit projection. The viewer belongs here, not in Eon or Orbit.
- EONW v5 `Snapshot.entries` already supplies every enabled popup entry's label and normalized physical shortcut; no protocol field or version is needed.
- `README.md:253-266` and VEN-C8 document positional tabs, workspace actions, F6, Escape, and catalog shortcuts. `README.md:110-117,311-312` documents host link and clipboard shortcuts.
- VEN-C18 proves native shared-popup geometry and focus, but its terminal popup is an Eon/Orbit Session. Reusing that lifecycle for help would add a process and duplicate native binding truth.

## Reference gate

Before implementation, read and record:

- Complete VEN-C2, VEN-C4, VEN-C5, VEN-C8, VEN-C10, VEN-C18, current key dispatch/release capture, scene/render layering, resize, notice, focus, and AccessKit owners.
- Exact EONW v5 snapshot/catalog definitions and Eon's collision-validation contract.
- GNOME/GTK application shortcut-window guidance as the primary comparable for a persistent, grouped, dismissible reference.
- One momentary shortcut-overlay comparable such as KeyCue or which-key only to record why held/timed presentation is deferred, not to import a prefix-key model.
- Current native popup and narrow/tiny-window proofs so the viewer reuses established typography, colors, clipping, and modal focus behavior without becoming a terminal popup.

Adopt a native Venus overlay, live EONW catalog rows, one local owner for fixed binding descriptors, explicit toggle/Escape dismissal, responsive grouping, and AccessKit dialog semantics.

Reject a generated Markdown page, terminal subprocess, webview, config parser in Venus, duplicate shortcut strings, searchable command palette, rebinding editor, action launcher, tutorial flow, bare-modifier interception, delayed timers, and a second viewer implementation. No dependency is selected.

## Scope

In scope:

- One ephemeral native viewer state owned by Venus.
- `Alt+Slash` toggle and Escape dismissal with exact press/release capture.
- A compact fixed-binding descriptor owner sufficient for both dispatch and display; keep specialized action logic specialized rather than building a generic command framework.
- Dynamic popup rows from the accepted snapshot.
- Responsive single-/multi-column or scrollable layout using existing shaping/rendering primitives.
- Pointer-safe modal behavior and a complete AccessKit projection with deterministic focus restoration.
- VEN-C20, README usage, changelog after accepted behavior, and exact LOC scorecard.

Out of scope:

- Eon catalog/configuration changes, component pinning, installed full-Eon acceptance, EONW changes, Orbit work, or another dependency.
- Search, filtering, editing, rebinding, executing a row, mouse-driven commands, tutorials, telemetry, persisted viewer state, or generalized modal framework.
- Child-application bindings or context inference inside a terminal application.
- Momentary peek in this slice. Create a later issue only after toggle-viewer dogfood shows a concrete need.
- macOS support or claims; keep the implementation platform-neutral where existing APIs allow and prove the currently supported Linux Wayland surface.

## Implementation notes

1. Add one deterministic red test for the viewer state transition, shortcut capture, effective row composition, dynamic entry refresh, and no workspace/terminal action.
2. Give the fixed native bindings one minimal descriptor owner used by recognition and viewer rows. Preserve dynamic targets such as the active tab and positional tab lookup without introducing closures, trait objects, or a generic command registry unless the existing types require them.
3. Project the viewer from current state through the existing scene/render/accessibility pipeline. Use existing text shaping, colors, bounds, clipping, scale, and focus machinery.
4. While open, consume input locally; `Alt+Slash` and Escape dismiss. Preserve matching releases, window focus loss, resize, reconnect, and prior-focus restoration.
5. Update VEN-C20/current docs only after behavior is proved. Record why momentary peek remains deferred or, after explicit user acceptance, plan it separately.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Alt+Slash` opens one viewer from terminal, workspace chrome, popup, pending-tab, and popup-only states; the same chord and Escape close it. Repeated press events do not toggle twice, and no captured press/release reaches Orbit.
- The viewer shows every current fixed Venus/Eon-surface shortcut exactly once with a concise action label, plus every enabled `Snapshot.entries` item using its exact current label and normalized shortcut. Disabled/absent catalog items disappear after refresh.
- Dispatch and displayed fixed chords share one code owner. A focused test fails if a displayed fixed binding and its recognized chord diverge. Venus does not parse Eon configuration or duplicate popup labels/shortcuts.
- Child-application shortcuts are excluded and clearly bounded; Yazi F1 and other app-owned help continue to reach the terminal when the viewer is closed.
- Viewer state is ephemeral and local: opening, refreshing, and closing change no Eon snapshot, selection, popup instance, Session, pane, tab, launch directory, clipboard, or link state.
- Normal, narrow, tiny, scaled, long-label, and maximum 32-entry snapshots remain dismissible and readable through bounded layout/scrolling without text escaping its surface.
- AccessKit exposes one labeled help dialog with grouped shortcut/action pairs, keyboard focus enters it, Escape closes it, and the prior valid terminal/chrome focus is restored.
- Existing terminal input, copy/paste, hyperlink, workspace, popup, focus, resize, recovery, and accessibility checks remain green.
- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, README LOC verification, and `git diff --check` pass on one unchanged candidate.
- An isolated native Linux Wayland observation verifies open, update, narrow resize, accessible navigation, dismissal, focus restoration, and no terminal input leakage. Record exact source, Eon/EONW fixture, compositor, scale, and remaining platform gaps.

## Stop conditions

- Stop if the implementation requires EONW changes, Eon-owned viewer state, an Orbit Session, child-application introspection, a new dependency, or a general command/rebinding system.
- Stop before choosing a different global chord; Eon must reserve the final chord before full-product delivery.
- Stop if the fixed shortcut refactor increases ownership or complexity more than a bounded local descriptor table; do not force unrelated terminal editing semantics through one registry.
- Stop if another active Venus frontier owns application input, workspace scene, rendering, or accessibility.

title: Traverse Eon tabs while preserving a tab-bound picker
description:
## User-visible contract

Consumer: one person using a live full-Eon Venus workspace with a directory picker open.

Trigger: the person presses existing Alt+H or Alt+L while the picker-owning tab is active, or again while another tab is active and that picker remains live.

Result: Venus sends the existing EONW v4 semantic focus-left or focus-right action. Accepted state presents the adjacent or wrapped active tab. Venus shows the picker endpoint only when its owning tab is active; another active tab shows its selected durable pane. Returning presents the same picker without cancelling, accepting, moving, or duplicating it.

Important failures: singleton traversal keeps the existing bounded Eon failure. Picker disappearance, stale snapshots, unavailable endpoints, failed actions, and attachment transitions preserve the last accepted coherent view. Up/down, focus-by-identity, creation, picker duplication, and unrelated topology changes gain no picker-visible exception.

Ownership: Venus owns shortcut admission and active-tab endpoint, scene, focus, metadata, input, and accessibility projection. Eon owns topology, picker lifecycle, and action acceptance. Orbit owns both picker and durable terminal Sessions.

## Contract routing

- Change VEN-C18 so picker presence is lifecycle truth while picker visibility is derived from `picker.tab == active_tab`.
- Preserve VEN-C8 durable-workspace projection and its ordinary shortcuts outside visible picker presentation.
- Consume EON-C18 owner proof `963bdaf4d9816f27a26c7bdb6ee122855566a222` and EON-C8 wrapped traversal source `5f23a7bac127785d913a718e5fb1afc53d9d91ae`. No Orbit contract changes.
- Platform disposition: neutral model, scene, and shortcut policy with an isolated Wayland dependency for native Venus proof.

## Prerequisites and reference gate

The EONW prerequisite is satisfied: Eon Bead `eon-allow-inactive-picker-snapshot-2u0` is closed at exact proof `963bdaf4d9816f27a26c7bdb6ee122855566a222`, published on Eon `edge` and accepted by Eon revision `9a56aeb18fc83dccbcf8887f63cc17a08d3cbf53`.

Required before code: VEN-C8 and VEN-C18; the relevant picker route in `docs/REFERENCES.md`; current `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`; complete model, application, scene, transport, shortcut, focus, metadata, accessibility, and tests; exact accepted Venus source `bdd8b3628452b1dba8c4d4b2ad9bc2e802659d29`; the two exact Eon proofs above; and Eon producer Bead `eon-traverse-tabs-during-picker-nxp` only to preserve the owner-consumer-acceptance sequence.

Dependency disposition: this is an exact revision-only update of the existing `eon-workspace-protocol` 0.1.0 Git dependency, not a dependency selection. Before manifest edits, record that its package, version, API owner, and dependency graph remain unchanged. The user already authorized this exact cross-repository consumer step; stop if the lock graph or ownership changes beyond the source revision.

Reuse the existing semantic Focus actions, attachment transition, and Unix-socket workspace substitute. Reject a new shortcut, action, protocol mirror, stored visibility state, optimistic topology, native picker, hidden fork, Orbit change, generic modal, checked-in fake server, or dependency.

## Scope boundary

In scope: the exact EONW Cargo and lock pin, one derived visible-picker predicate, active attachment and scene projection, existing Alt+H/L admission, focused model/application/scene/metadata/accessibility/transport checks, VEN-C8/VEN-C18/current reference and user docs, changelog after accepted behavior, README LOC, and isolated native Venus proof against a disposable protocol-faithful workspace substitute.

Out of scope: the Eon producer, Eon component manifest, installed full-Eon profile or end-to-end claim, Orbit, picker editing, up/down exception, new keybinding, configuration, dependency choice, module, platform expansion, or persistent test backend. The later Eon producer Bead consumes the accepted Venus source and owns installed full-product dogfood.

## Acceptance Criteria

The structured acceptance criteria field is canonical.
design:
1. Pin exact EONW proof `963bdaf4d9816f27a26c7bdb6ee122855566a222`; verify the lock changes only that existing Git source and package identity.
2. Update VEN-C18, VEN-C8 consumed identity, and stale active-picker wording in current reference/user docs before production code.
3. Extend the smallest existing tests at each changed owner: shortcut admission, model attachment, scene/accessibility, metadata visibility, and transport ordering. Reuse the current UnixListener substitute only for exact Focus action and snapshot exchange; add no cross-module harness or broad fixture.
4. Replace the misleading global `directory_picker_active` query with one pure derived `directory_picker_visible` predicate (`picker.tab == active_tab`) at the lowest existing shared Venus boundary. Reuse it for attachment, scene, focus, metadata, input, and accessibility. Lifecycle presence remains the canonical snapshot field; add no second presence query, stored state, type, or module.
5. Admit only left/right as picker-visible shortcut exceptions. When the picker is inactive, ordinary shortcut admission may proceed and Eon remains the topology-policy owner.
6. Run focused and complete locked Rust checks. Use a disposable protocol-faithful workspace substitute for one isolated native Wayland Venus observation; it proves consumer presentation and input only, not Eon producer or full-product behavior.
7. Commit one exact accepted Venus source for Eon to pin. The later Eon Bead implements action admission, updates the component graph/profile, and performs installed end-to-end dogfood.
acceptance_criteria:
1. With the picker-owning tab active or inactive, Alt+H/L sends the existing EONW v4 Focus Left/Right action. Non-workspace terminal keys continue to reach the currently attached picker or durable terminal through existing input routing.
2. An accepted adjacent or wrapped tab snapshot detaches the visible picker and attaches the active tab's selected durable pane without stopping either Session.
3. While another tab is active, the picker remains in the snapshot but contributes no terminal geometry, does not suppress active-pane metadata, and owns neither input focus nor accessibility. Alt+H/L remains admitted there so returning reattaches the identical picker endpoint and restores modal presentation.
4. Only left/right gain a picker-visible Venus shortcut exception. Up/down, focus-by-identity, create pane/tab, picker duplication, and unrelated mutations retain current admission or bounded Eon rejection without optimistic topology or a changed accepted snapshot.
5. Singleton, stale, lost, unavailable, duplicate, and failed attachment transitions remain bounded and do not create a second endpoint, picker, schema, action, or topology owner.
6. `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` consume exact EONW proof `963bdaf4d9816f27a26c7bdb6ee122855566a222`; the existing package/version and dependency graph otherwise remain unchanged.
7. Existing focused checks prove each changed predicate consumer; the current protocol-faithful Unix-socket substitute proves exact Focus action and snapshot ordering. No cross-module harness or broad fixture is added, and complete locked Rust checks pass.
8. Isolated native Wayland Venus dogfood against a disposable substitute proves visible/inactive/return presentation, attachment, input, focus, metadata, and accessibility. It makes no Eon producer, installed full-Eon, or end-to-end behavior claim.
9. VEN-C18 records the changed visibility contract, VEN-C8 records the exact consumed EONW identity, stale active-picker wording is removed from current docs, and the accepted source commit becomes the only Venus handoff to the Eon producer Bead.
10. No new action, keybinding, protocol version, dependency, configuration, module, Orbit behavior, stored visibility state, checked-in fake backend, or platform surface is added; changelog after accepted behavior, README LOC, Beads state, and final diff are exact.

title: Allow callers to disable native window decorations
description:
## Why

Venus always requests a decorated native window, so users cannot opt out of the desktop title bar even when Eon already provides its own workspace chrome. The user chose an explicit way to disable the native window bar, not a new undecorated default.

Smallest observable contract:
- Consumer: a direct Venus launcher or an Eon composition that supplies Venus launch arguments.
- Trigger: launch Venus with an explicit no-decorations option.
- Result: Venus requests an undecorated native window before creation. Without the option, the existing decorated default is unchanged.
- Invalid options fail immediately with bounded usage text before any window or transport is created.
- The first proof is Linux Wayland/X11. Other platforms remain architecture targets and may follow exact winit behavior until separately proved.

Contract routing:
- Add one user-approved VEN-C9 launch/presentation contract before implementation because the option is a new consumer-visible surface.
- Preserve VEN-C1 through VEN-C4, VEN-C7, VEN-C8, every Orbit/Eon protocol, native content geometry, and lifecycle.
- This Venus Bead supplies only the native capability. A persistent Eon product setting is owned by Eon and requires separate Eon planning; do not create a Venus settings system.

## Evidence

- `src/main.rs:118-129` creates `Window::default_attributes()` without overriding decorations, so exact winit 0.30.13 keeps its `true` default.
- `src/main.rs:1048-1055` accepts only zero, one, or two positional socket arguments and has no launch option.
- Exact locked winit 0.30.13 `src/window.rs:350-358` provides `WindowAttributes::with_decorations(bool)`; `src/window.rs:1150-1168` documents server- or winit-provided decorations and the decorated default.
- Exact winit Wayland support requests and hides client/server decorations through the existing backend; X11 uses the existing Motif decoration hint. No new dependency or custom titlebar is required.
- `README.md:89-96` records configuration and settings as outside the current slice, so the minimum Venus-owned surface is a launch option rather than a config file.

Impact: MED for focused and tiling-window workflows.
Effort: S.
Implementation risk: MED because undecorated windows intentionally lose native title-bar close and drag affordances.
Confidence: HIGH for the native capability and MED for later Eon configuration UX.

## Scope

In scope:
- Minimal launch-option parsing in `src/main.rs` using existing standard-library argument handling.
- Apply the chosen boolean through exact winit `WindowAttributes::with_decorations` before window creation.
- Focused parsing/default tests, bounded usage text, README run documentation, new VEN-C9 contract/proof, and LOC accounting.
- Native Linux Wayland dogfood; X11 dogfood when available.

Out of scope:
- Changing the default; runtime toggling; custom client-side titlebars; new close, drag, maximize, or minimize controls; keyboard shortcuts; persistence; a Venus config file; or a CLI parsing dependency.
- Eon config-schema or launcher changes, window transparency, fullscreen, size, position, theme, tab/pane chrome, macOS implementation, or protocol changes.

## References Before Code

Required:
- Current `src/main.rs` window and argument owners, README run surface, contracts, and `docs/CRATES.md`.
- Exact locked winit 0.30.13 `WindowAttributes::with_decorations`, `Window::set_decorations`, Wayland decoration, and X11 decoration-hint implementations.

Comparison only:
- Current desktop environment behavior for decorated and undecorated Eon windows. No external terminal implementation is needed for this one native capability.

Rejected:
- Permanently removing decorations, building an Eon-owned titlebar first, runtime decoration toggles, environment-variable policy, a general settings framework, or adding a CLI parser crate for one boolean.

Platform classification:
- Isolated platform dependency. Winit owns the native request. Linux is proved first; macOS feasibility is preserved but runtime behavior remains unproved.

## Acceptance and Verification

- Launch with no decoration option produces the same decorated request as today.
- The explicit option produces a window created with decorations disabled.
- The option works with the default socket and both accepted positional socket forms.
- Unknown options and excess positional arguments fail before window creation with current, deterministic usage text.
- Existing socket paths, Wayland application identity, accessibility adapter, renderer initialization, IME, resize, close handling, and workspace/Orbit behavior remain unchanged.
- No dependency, config file, runtime toggle, or custom window control is added.
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo check --locked`
- `cargo test --locked`
- `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `git diff --check`
- Native Wayland dogfood verifies decorated default and explicit borderless launch. Verify X11 when available and record any window-manager hint limitation.
- Promote VEN-C9 only against the exact proof-bearing commit; retain all consumed Eon and Orbit revisions.

## Stop Conditions

- Stop for user choice if a complete useful result requires a persistent Eon setting rather than the bounded Venus launch capability.
- Stop if a supported Linux backend cannot honor the request through existing winit without custom decorations.
- Stop before adding replacement close/drag controls, a settings owner, another dependency, or cross-repository implementation.
- Stop if source or proof revisions drift materially before implementation.

## Maintenance Notes

The default stays decorated because it preserves native close and drag affordances. Borderless mode is an explicit opt-in and may rely on desktop shortcuts for movement and closure. Add Eon configuration only in an Eon-owned follow-up after the launch capability proves useful.

title: Prove Venus as a thin native client for Orbit

design:
